title: Using FMAX
summary: FMAX lets you edit player, club, and competition values live while FM27 is running. This wiki covers everything from initial setup to every screen in the app.
text: The FMAX home screen. Pick a category on the left, then click a name in the list to open an edit tab. FMAX was previously called FMLE. If you were already using FMLE, just update—it switches over to FMAX automatically and keeps all your settings and history. New to FMAX? If this is your first time using FMAX, follow the two pages below in order. You'll go from installing the app to saving your first edit in about 10 minutes. Getting started Install FMAX, connect to FM27, and save your first edit. When edits take effect What applies right away, what needs saving, and what stays in your save file. What you can do Editing players Edit almost every detail of a player—attributes, positions, contracts, relationships, and languages. Game editor (⚡) Complete transfers and loans, clear injuries, remove unhappiness, terminate contracts, and set homegrown status immediately without advancing a day. Live tweaks Rules that keep working while switched on—growth and aging rules, Prevent retirement, preventing manager sackings, and more. Eri Ask your AI analyst questions and get transfer targets and to-dos as cards. Shortlist Gather players and staff into lists, and import or export them as game shortlist files. Tactic Arena Run hundreds of simulated matches inside the game with your tactic files and rank them by points to see which is strongest. Official tests & Tactic Lab Measure your tactic under identical conditions in an Official test and upload the results to the Tactic Lab. FAQ Administrator permissions, using FMAX alongside other mods, how long edits stick, and more.

title: Getting started
summary: Follow step by step from installing FMAX and connecting to FM27 to editing a player's value and saving it into the game.

3. Open FMAX and check the connection
4. Open a player from the list
When the Save button is disabled
Keeping changes in your save file
text: What you need - Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) - Football Manager 27 (FM27) version 27.0.1+2503222 . FMAX won't connect if your game version is different. - Before making your first edits, it's a good idea to back up a copy of your save. Once you save your game in FM, edited values remain in the save file. 1. Install FMAX 1. Download FMAX-setup.exe from getfmax.com. 2. Run the file—it downloads the latest version and opens the setup wizard. Click Next → Install → Finish . 3. FMAX is added to your Start menu. For details on the blue "Windows protected your PC" prompt, whether administrator rights are needed, and more, see Installing, updating and uninstalling. 2. Launch FM27 and load a save Open FM27 and load a save as usual. FMAX reads and writes data in whichever save is currently open in the game, whether it's a new game or an ongoing career. You can also open FMAX first. Once you launch FM27 and load a save, FMAX connects automatically. 3. Open FMAX and check the connection Launch FMAX from the Start menu or your desktop. A startup screen appears first and checks off three stages in order. Stage What happens Preparing FMAX FMAX sets up the interface. Finding game Looks for a running copy of FM27. Once found, this changes to 'Find game · FM27 connected'. Reading game Reads every list from the game for the first time, showing progress as a percentage. Once reading finishes, the startup screen closes and the list screen opens. If it takes a while, click Continue without waiting at the bottom to head straight in while reading finishes in the background. If FM27 isn't running or you haven't loaded a save yet, the startup screen lets you know and moves on to the list screen after a moment. Leave FMAX open and load your save in the game. Reading the connection badge The pill badge in the top-right corner of the window shows your live connection status. A green dot with FM27 connected means everything is ready. Badge Meaning What to do Checking Looking for the game. Wait a moment. FM27 closed FM27 is not running. Launch the game and load a save—FMAX connects automatically. FM27 starting The game is still starting up. FMAX connects automatically once the main menu loads. Waiting for save No save loaded yet. Load a save and FMAX reads it automatically. Reading Reading game data for the first time. Once finished, lists and tabs open right away with no wait. FM27 connected Connected to FM27. You're ready to read and edit values. Version mismatch Unsupported game version. See Troubleshooting. No access Can’t open the game. If you ran FM27 as administrator, run FMAX as administrator too. Error Something went wrong while reading the game. Wait a moment and try again. Click the badge to open the Connection status popup. The Connection status popup, showing the active save name, the game version FMAX supports, and the count and timestamp for each loaded list. - Current save: The save currently open in the game. - Game version: The FM27 build FMAX is able to read. - Player, Staff, Club …: How many items were read for each type and when. - Writing: Shows 'Only if read values haven’t changed' when connected. FMAX only writes when the in-game value still matches what FMAX read on screen. - Reload from game (when connected) / Check again (when disconnected): Re-reads data from the game, or looks for the game again. - Developer log — Save log · Copy: Diagnostic log to send to the developer if something goes wrong. See Troubleshooting. 4. Open a player from the list The list screen. Pick a category on the left, then click a name in the middle list to open an edit tab. 1. Under Game data on the left, click Player . The number next to each category is how many items were read from the game. 2. Type a player's name into the search box at the top. 3. Click the player's row in the list. A tab for that player appears across the top and opens their edit screen. Clicking the checkbox at the left of a row selects the player without opening a tab. To select and edit multiple people at once, see Using lists. You can also jump straight to whoever you're viewing in FM27. With a player, staff, club or team screen open in FM27, click Open viewed screen (the monitor icon) at the top of FMAX or press Ctrl+G . 5. Edit a value The Attributes view on a Player tab. Click any field to edit it in place. 1. Select Attributes on the left side of the tab. 2. Click the attribute you want to change (for example, Crossing). − , the number, and + appear in place of the value. 3. Change the number: - Click − / + , or type a number directly. - Press ↑ ↓ or scroll the mouse wheel to step by 1. Hold Shift for larger steps (5 at a time for attributes). 4. Press Enter or click elsewhere to confirm. Esc cancels the edit you just made, and Tab confirms and moves to the next field. Edited fields show the original value in small text beside the new one. At the bottom of the tab, an N changes bar appears, previewing the first two edits such as 'Crossing 19→20'. The 'internal' number shown while editing an attribute is the finer-grained value the game stores behind the 1–20 rating on screen. If you set the attribute back to its original rating, FMAX preserves the game's original fine-grained value. So far, this has only changed on screen in FMAX. Click Save to write it into the game. After editing a single value: the changes bar and Save button appear at the bottom of the tab, and a Save button with your total change count appears at the top of the window. 6. Save to the game There are two Save buttons: Button Location What it writes Save Bottom changes bar of the active tab Writes only the edits made on this tab to the game. Save N (Save all) Top-right of the window Writes edits across every open tab, one tab after another. N is the total number of edited values. Ctrl+S does the same. The top Save N button only appears when you have unsaved edits. Pressing Ctrl+S when nothing has changed lets you know there's nothing to save. When you click Save, FMAX:

title: Installing, updating and uninstalling
summary: Install FMAX without administrator rights using a single installer, update from inside the app after confirming, and see what to keep in mind when uninstalling.
text: What you need - Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) - FM27 version 27.0.1+2503222 . FMAX won't connect if your game version is different. FMAX never modifies your game files on disk. It reads and writes values in the running game while FMAX is open. Downloading the installer The only file you need to download is FMAX-setup.exe from getfmax.com . It's a lightweight installer: every time you run it, it downloads the newest version, verifies its signature, and opens the setup wizard. Even if you re-run an older copy of FMAX-setup.exe months later, it will still fetch and install whatever version is latest then. Files downloaded from other sources won't pass FMAX's signature check. Installing 1. Run the downloaded FMAX-setup.exe . 2. If the blue "Windows protected your PC" screen appears, click More info and then Run anyway . 3. A small window appears briefly while the latest version downloads, followed by the setup wizard. Click Next → Install → Finish . Leave Create Desktop Shortcut checked on the final screen if you'd also like FMAX on your desktop. The "Windows protected your PC" warning appears because FMAX does not use a paid code-signing certificate. As long as you downloaded the installer from getfmax.com, it is safe to run. Your browser may show a similar prompt during download. Here is what installation sets up: - Installs only to your own Windows user account ( %LOCALAPPDATA%\FMAX ). Administrator rights are not required. - Adds FMAX to the Start menu. - Registers FMAX under Windows Settings → Apps → Installed apps , which is where you uninstall it. Once installed, head over to Getting started. Keep all files in the installation folder together. Do not move fmax.exe on its own to another folder or mix files from different versions. If required files are missing or damaged, FMAX stops on startup and lets you know. Reinstall using the installer from the Releases page above, leaving "Delete application data" unchecked so your settings and lists stay intact. Updating to a new version A few seconds after opening, an installed copy of FMAX checks once for updates. When a new version is out, a "New version … is available · Current version is …" banner appears for 30 seconds with an Install button. 1. Click Install on the notification. 2. A confirmation dialog asks "Update to version …?" Click Install to go ahead, or Later to skip for now. 3. 'Downloading update' appears along with download progress (%). 4. 'Preparing installation · FMAX will close and restart shortly' appears, and FMAX closes. 5. Once installation finishes, the updated FMAX launches automatically. During an update, FMAX takes care of the following: - It installs the update only after verifying its digital signature to confirm the file genuinely came from FMAX. If the signature doesn't match, installation is aborted. - Before closing, FMAX temporarily lifts any Live tweaks and game rules it had active. When the new version opens, they turn back on according to Restore previous state on launch in Settings. If that setting is turned off, everything starts paused so you can re-enable them on each screen. - If you were using Keep men’s team eligibility, FMAX may ask you to reload your save after restarting. - Everything FMAX remembers—Settings, presets, Shortlist, and your Live tweaks and Locks lists—carries over untouched. If you missed the banner or clicked Later , FMAX will notify you again the next time you open it. Updating manually Downloading and running a fresh installer from the Releases page updates FMAX in the exact same way, keeping all your settings and lists. If an uninstall screen pops up during setup, do not check "Delete application data" . Checking it wipes all settings and lists FMAX has saved. Checking your current version Open Update notes under Tools on the left to see your installed version number, marked with a 'Current' badge in the release list. You can also see what changed in each release there (Settings and Update notes). When an update fails If an update can't be installed, FMAX shows 'Couldn't install the update' along with the reason. Reason What to do Please check your internet connection. Couldn't download the update. Check your connection and try again. The signature didn’t match, so it wasn’t installed. The downloaded file couldn't be verified as genuine FMAX, so nothing was installed. Your current FMAX is untouched. Couldn’t restore the game code. Please restart FMAX. Setup stopped because active Live tweaks couldn't be removed cleanly. Restart FMAX and try again. Couldn’t open the installer. Please restart FMAX. Restart FMAX and try again. If it keeps happening, download and run FMAX-setup.exe from getfmax.com. An installation is already in progress. An update is already running—wait for it to finish. You’re already on the latest version. There is no newer version to download. manifest_policy The new release targets a game version your current FMAX (or FMLE) doesn't recognise, so in-app update skipped it. This happens when FM is patched and FMAX releases a build for the new game patch. Download and run FMAX-setup.exe from getfmax.com—it installs cleanly on top and keeps your settings, lists, Live tweaks and Locks. Clicking update in FMLE for 27.0.0 (up to version 26.1108) shows manifest_policy . Run FMAX-setup.exe once as described above to upgrade. Upgrading from FMLE to FMAX FMLE was FMAX's earlier name. Updating from FMLE to an FMAX release makes these changes: - FMAX installs into a new folder ( %LOCALAPPDATA%\FMAX ). - FMLE shortcuts on your desktop and Start menu are replaced with FMAX shortcuts. Shortcuts pointing to an FMLE copy in another location are left alone. - Program files in the old folder ( %LOCALAPPDATA%\FMLE ) and the FMLE uninstall entry are removed. If you placed any personal files in that folder, the folder and your files are kept. - Your settings, lists, Live tweaks, Locks and records carry over automatically. Uninstalling 1. title: Screen overview
summary: A tour of the FMAX window—the top tab bar, left sidebar, lists, edit tabs, and bottom status bar.
text: The main screen when you open FMAX, with the tab bar across the top, the sidebar on the left, and the selected list on the right. The FMAX window is split into four parts: 1. Top tab bar : The "List" button, your open edit tabs, and controls like Save and Connection status. 2. Left sidebar : Categories to browse (Player, Club, and more) and tools (Live tweaks, Locks, and more). Shown only when viewing lists or tools. 3. Main area : Displays the list or tool chosen in the sidebar, or the active edit tab. 4. Bottom bar : Shows item counts, selections, and pending unsaved edits. Top tab bar From left to right: Button What it does List (FMAX logo) Returns to the list view while keeping your open tabs intact. Open tabs Each player, club, or other item opens in its own tab. Click to switch tabs or drag to reorder them. When many tabs are open, they narrow down to show just faces or logos. See Tabs and quick open. + (Open in a tab) Search by name to open a new tab. Same as Ctrl+K . Close all tabs Appears next to + when two or more tabs are open. Closes all tabs and returns to the list view. Ctrl+Shift+W Save (number) Appears only when you have unsaved edits. The number shows the total count of edited fields across all open tabs. Click to write every tab's changes to the game at once. Ctrl+S (When changes are written to the game) Locks (number) Appears when any values are locked—for example, "Locks 3", or "Locks 3 · Stopped" when paused. Click to open the Locks screen. Eri (face icon) Opens or closes the chat panel for AI analyst Eri. Ctrl+J Open viewed screen (monitor) Opens whichever player, staff member, club, or team you're currently viewing in FM as a tab in FMAX, without changing any game data. Ctrl+G Theme (moon / sun) Switches between dark mode and light mode. Connection indicator Shows the live connection state with FM. Click to open the Connection status popup (see below). Minimize · Maximize · Close Standard window controls. Drag an empty spot on the tab bar to move the window, or double-click it to maximize. If you click Open viewed screen while viewing a screen FMAX can't open directly—such as a competition, nation, or match screen—FMAX lets you know. Open a player, staff, club, or team screen in FM first and try again. Connection indicator FMAX checks for FM every 5 seconds and updates the connection indicator accordingly. Status Meaning FM27 connected Connected to the game and ready to read and write values. Reading (%) Reading the save for the first time. Once finished, lists and tabs open without waiting. Waiting for save FM is running, but no save is loaded yet. FMAX reads it automatically once you load one. FM27 starting FM is launching. FMAX connects automatically once the game reaches the main menu. FM27 closed FM isn't running. Launch the game and load a save to connect automatically. Version mismatch Your game version isn't supported by this version of FMAX. A notice also appears at the bottom of the sidebar. No access If FM was launched as administrator, run FMAX as administrator too. Error Something went wrong while reading the game. Wait a moment and try again. Checking FMAX just started and is looking for the game. Clicking the connection indicator opens the Connection status popup. The Connection status popup shows: - Current save : The name FMAX detected for the loaded save. A brand-new game that hasn't been saved yet appears as "Unsaved new game" (What each save remembers separately). - Game version : The FM version FMAX is reading. - Item counts and last-read times for each category (for example, "Player 108,457 · 14:38"). - Writing : "Only if read values haven’t changed" means FMAX writes an edit only if the game's current value still matches what FMAX originally read (When changes are written to the game). - Reload from game button (or "Check again" when disconnected): Re-reads all lists and open tabs from the game. - Save / Copy Developer log : Saves or copies a diagnostic log (Save log / Copy log) to your Downloads folder or clipboard to send to the developer if loading fails. Theme Click the theme button to toggle between dark mode and light mode. FMAX follows your Windows theme at first, then remembers your choice across restarts. Separate windows like the filter window follow the same theme. You can toggle the translucent "glass effect" for bars and panels in Settings. Left sidebar Scrolling down the sidebar reveals My manager & club, Favourites, and Recent edits. Game data Lists for Player, Staff, Support staff, Club, Nation, Competition, City, Stadium, Team, Agent, Referee, and Agreement. The number next to each name is the count read from the game. Click any category to open its list on the right (Using lists). Languages aren't listed in the sidebar—press Ctrl+K and search for a language by name to open it in a tab. Tools Tool What it does Eri Ask the AI analyst questions and get scouting suggestions and action cards. Eri Shortlist Group players and staff into named lists and exchange .fmf shortlist files with FM. Shortlist Presets Create and manage reusable bundles that edit multiple fields at once. Presets Locks Keep chosen values pinned even when the game tries to change them. The number shows how many values are locked. Locks Compare View two open tabs of the same type side by side. Compare Record room Browse Season stats and historical records. Stats, player cards & Record room Live tweaks Ongoing enhancements that stay active while switched on. Shows the count of active tweaks when enabled. Live tweaks Korean names Gives regens Korean names (shown only when FMAX is in Korean). Korean names Settings Configure FMAX settings. Settings and Update notes Update notes See what changed in each release. Settings and Update notes My manager & club Shown whenever the save has a human-controlled manager. title: Using lists
summary: How to search, filter, sort, choose columns, export to CSV, and work with multiple items at once in lists like Players and Clubs.
heads: Saved filters in the filter window
text: The Player list, with the search box and toolbar buttons at the top, column headers below, and the item count at the bottom. Opening a list Click any category under "Game data" in the left sidebar to open its list. The number next to each name shows how many entries FMAX read from the game. When FMAX connects to the game, it reads every list once up front. While that's happening, a banner like "Reading Player list for the first time" appears above the list. Once that initial read finishes, switching between lists is instant. Any remaining fields (columns not currently shown) continue loading in the background, so adding columns or filtering later stays fast. If you turn off "When connected to the game, read lists immediately" in Settings, FMAX waits until you open a list or click Reload. The "Shortlist" screen under Tools works just like the lists described here. It shows only the people on the chosen shortlist, and remembers its columns, sort order, and filters separately from the main Player and Staff lists. For the bar used to create and switch shortlists, see Shortlist. Lists themselves are read-only. To edit values, click a row to open its edit tab, or select multiple rows and apply a preset (Selecting multiple rows). Buttons above the list Button What it does Search box Finds items by name. Search Filter Opens the filter window. When conditions are active, the button shows how many are applied. Ctrl+Shift+F Filter Saved filters Picks a saved filter and applies it right away. Saved filters Columns Chooses which columns to show and their order. Choosing columns CSV Saves the current list view as a CSV file (for Excel). Exporting to CSV Reload (circular arrow) Reloads every list and open tab from the game. Reloading ? Help Opens this page. F1 Search Start typing a name in the search box and the list filters immediately. Case and accents (such as é or ñ) are ignored. Press Ctrl+F to jump straight to the search box. Besides names, search also checks the fields below depending on the list: List Also searches Player Club, Nationality Staff Club, Nationality, Full name Support staff Club, Nationality, Unique ID Club Short name, Nation, City Team Club, League Nation Short name, 3-letter code City Nation, Region Competition Short name, Abbreviation, Nation Stadium Continental competition name, City, Owner club Agent Nationality, Based nation Referee Nationality, Home city Agreement Short name You can also search by Unique ID, with or without the r- prefix used for regens (such as r-12345 ). Search works alongside any active filters. Your search text is kept only while FMAX stays open. Sorting Click any column header to sort by that column. Each click cycles through three states: 1. First click: highest to lowest for numbers, or A to Z for text. 2. Second click: reverse order. 3. Third click: clears sorting. An arrow appears next to the sorted column header. Rows with empty values always stay at the bottom regardless of sort direction. By default, each list starts sorted highest to lowest by its main column (such as Current ability for Players and Reputation for Clubs). Choosing columns Clicking "Columns" lets you reorder columns with the up and down arrows or remove them with ×. Clicking "Columns" opens the "Visible columns" popup. - Up and down arrows : Move that column one place earlier or later. - × : Remove that column. The Name column can't be removed, though you can move it. - Add column : Opens the field picker. Type in "Search fields" at the top, or browse the categories (Frequently used, attribute groups, Overview, and more) and click a field to add it at the end. You can also navigate with ↑ and ↓ and press Enter to add. - Reset to default : Restores the default columns for that list. The "Frequently used" category includes values calculated by FMAX, such as Name, Age, Primary position, Recommended Current Ability (RCA), and Attribute effectiveness. Multi-row data (such as injury lists) can't be shown as list columns. Your chosen columns, column order, sort order, and filters are saved on this PC separately for each list, so they stay put when you restart FMAX or open another save. Clicking "Reset settings" in Settings resets columns, sorting, and filters across every list back to their defaults. Filter Filters narrow down a list using conditions like "Current ability at least 150" or "Unattached". Click Filter (or press Ctrl+Shift+F ) to open the separate filter window. The filter window, with Saved filters on the left, conditions in the middle, and the live match count at the top right. Filter window layout - Top bar : The "Filter" title, a dropdown for which list you're filtering (such as "Player list"), the theme toggle, and minimize and close buttons. - Match count : Updates live at the top right with how many items match your current conditions (for example, "120 / 108,457 players"). If FMAX hasn't read a required field yet, "Reading values from the game" appears briefly. - Quick filters : One-click buttons that add common conditions right away (see table below). - Player interest : Available only for the Player list (see below). - Conditions area : Where you add and edit filter conditions. - Bottom buttons : Clear all, Revert, and Apply to list. - Left "Saved filters" panel : Your saved filters, plus "Save current conditions", "Import", and "Export". Changes made in the filter window don't update the list in the main window until you click Apply to list . Until then, "Not applied to list yet" appears at the bottom. Building conditions 1. Click + Condition to open the field picker. 2. Find and choose the field to filter by (for example, Current ability). 3. Pick a Comparison option (At least, At most, Between, and so on). 4. Enter a value—or two values if you picked "Between". 5. Repeat from step 1 to add more conditions. 6. Click Apply to list (or press Ctrl+Enter , or press Enter inside a value box). Click the field name at the start of a condition row to swap it for a diff

title: Tabs, quick open, and right-click menu
summary: How to open, close, and reopen edit tabs, reorder tabs, jump anywhere with Ctrl+K quick open, use every option in the right-click menu, and save bookmarks.
heads: Clicking a name to jump to it
text: Every time you open an item such as a player or club, FMAX opens a tab for it in the top bar. Just like browser tabs, you can keep several open at once and switch between them. Tabs stay open until you close them, and come right back when you reopen FMAX. Opening tabs You can open a tab in any of these ways: - Click a row in a list, or highlight a row and press Enter . - Press Ctrl+K or click + in the tab bar for Quick open. - Click an underlined name (Clicking a name to jump to it). - Click an item under My manager & club, Bookmarks, or Recent edits in the sidebar. - Choose Open in a tab from the right-click menu. - Select multiple rows in a list and click Open in a tab in the bottom bar (up to 20 at once). - Click the Open viewed screen button ( Ctrl+G ) in the tab bar to open whichever player, staff member, club, or team you are currently viewing in FM27. Opening an item that already has a tab switches straight to that tab instead of creating a duplicate. Every time a tab opens, FMAX reads fresh data for that item from the game. Switching between tabs - Click any tab to switch to it. Click List on the far left to return to the list screen. - Ctrl+Tab moves to the next tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab moves to the previous one. The List screen counts as one stop. - Ctrl+1 goes to the List screen, Ctrl+2 – Ctrl+8 jump to the first through seventh tabs from the left, and Ctrl+9 jumps to the last tab. - When you have too many tabs to fit across the bar, scroll the mouse wheel over the tab bar to pan sideways. As you open more tabs, they narrow down; once narrow enough, only the face or club badge is shown without the name. Hover over a tab to see its full name and type, such as 'Lionel Messi · Player'. A tab with unsaved changes shows a purple dot where the close (×) button normally sits. Hover over it to reveal the × again. Reordering tabs Drag a tab left or right to change its order. Dragging only kicks in after moving a few pixels, so a normal click simply switches tabs. Your tab order is remembered when you restart FMAX. Closing tabs - Click × on a tab, or middle-click anywhere on the tab. - Ctrl+W : Closes the current tab. Does nothing on the List screen. - Close all tabs (appears next to + when two or more tabs are open) or Ctrl+Shift+W : Closes every open tab and returns to List. When you close several tabs in a row using ×, tab widths stay fixed until your cursor leaves the tab bar so the next × lands right under your pointer. If you close a tab with unsaved edits, those changes are not written to the game. A notice such as '2 unsaved changes discarded' appears—click 'Reopen' right away to get them back (see below). Reopening closed tabs Right after you close a tab, a Reopen button briefly appears in the notice. Click it or press Ctrl+Shift+T to bring the last closed tab back in its original spot, on the same subpage, complete with any unsaved edits. - Press Ctrl+Shift+T repeatedly to bring closed tabs back one by one in reverse order, up to the last 30 closes. - If you used 'Close all tabs', reopening restores the entire set at once and puts you back on the tab you were viewing. - A reopened tab reloads its data from the game. If any game values changed in the meantime, your unsaved edits are rechecked against the new values—and if the game already matches what you were going to set, that edit is dropped. - Closed-tab history is cleared when you quit FMAX. Quick open (Ctrl+K) Quick open brought up with Ctrl+K . Items that already have a tab are marked 'Already open'. Press Ctrl+K or click + in the tab bar from any screen to bring up a search box in the center of the window. 1. Type part of a name, or a unique ID (including regen IDs with r- ). 2. Matching items appear grouped by type—Player, Staff, Club, and more. Before you type anything, up to 4 items per type are shown; once you type, up to 8 per type appear. 3. Use ↑ ↓ and Enter , or click a result to open its tab. Press Esc , press Ctrl+K again, or click outside the box to close it. Quick open searches by name only (not by club or nationality). You can also find and open languages here, even though they don't have a list screen of their own. Until FMAX has loaded lists from the game, the box displays 'You can search once lists are read from the game'. Right-clicking a search result opens the right-click menu below. Right-click menu The right-click menu on a player row. Right-click anywhere that points to an item to open its context menu: - Rows in a list (right-clicking a linked name inside a row, such as a club or nationality, targets that club or nation) - Underlined names inside edit tabs, and rows in the squad or staff tables on a club tab - Quick open results, plus My manager & club, Bookmarks, and Recent edits in the sidebar With a keyboard, focus a list row or linked name and press the Menu key or Shift+F10 . Text inputs such as search boxes do not open this menu. The top of the menu shows the item's name and 'Player · ID 7458500'. If you right-click with multiple rows selected, the header shows '3 selected' and the action applies to all of them. Single and multiple selection Option What it does When written to game Open in a tab (multiple: Open in 3 tabs) Opens tabs for the selection, up to 20 at once (dimmed above 20). — Copy unique ID (multiple: Copy 3 unique IDs) Copies the unique ID ( r-12345 format for regens). Multiple IDs are copied One per line. — Add to shortlist Players and staff only. Pick a list or click 'Add to new list'. Anyone already on the list stays as is. Shortlist Does not write to the game. Remove from this list Shortlist screen only. Removes the selection from the current list. Does not write to the game. Add to bookmarks / Remove from bookmarks Single item only. Does not write to the game. Batch edits Option What it does When written to game Apply preset Pick a preset and apply it after a confirmation prompt. Presets Immediately on confirmation. Apply custom edit Opens the Presets screen as a New preset.

title: When changes take effect in the game
summary: What waits for Save, what applies right away, what needs the game date to advance, what requires saving in FM27 to keep, and how to revert changes.
heads: When the Save button is disabled
Live tweaks and My manager options
What never writes to the game
What takes effect when the game date advances
Saving in FM27 to keep your changes
If game values changed in the meantime
text: FMAX edits your running FM27 game directly, though when a change actually goes into the game depends on the feature you use. Here is how each one works. At a glance What you do When it enters the game How to undo Edits in an edit tab When you click Save at the bottom of the tab or Save at the top ( Ctrl+S ) Before saving: Revert button. After saving: edit the value back and save again Preset values filled into an edit tab When you click Save, as above Same as above Presets applied to multiple items from lists, right-click menus, or tables Right away when you click Apply in the confirmation prompt Once, via Revert in the notice ⚡ In-game editor actions Right away on confirmation None Live tweaks Continuously while FMAX is running (mostly as the game date advances) Turn off Locks While FMAX is running, re-applied whenever the game changes a value Unlock Shortlist, Bookmarks, Saved filters, creating presets Never written to the game — Whichever feature writes a value into the live game, you still need to save your game in FM27 for it to stay in your save file (below). Saving in edit tabs A player tab with one edited value, showing the '1 changed value' bar at the bottom and the 'Save 1' button at the top. Changes you make inside an edit tab don't go straight into the game—they wait in that tab until you save. - Edited rows are highlighted, and a bar appears at the bottom of the tab such as 2 changed values Crossing 19→20, Passing 17→18 (with '+N more' if you changed more than three). The bar has Revert and Save buttons. - In the top tab bar, that tab shows a purple dot in place of its × button. - At the top right, a Save button appears with the total count of pending edits across every open tab. Everything you edit inside an edit tab—attributes, contracts, info, relationships, Injuries & bans lists, Nationality & City of birth—only goes into the game when you press 'Save'. How to save - Save at the bottom of the tab : Writes only the edits in this tab. - Save at the top or Ctrl+S : Saves every tab with pending edits, one tab at a time. If nothing has changed, FMAX tells you there is nothing to save. When you press Save, the bar shows 'Writing to game · Check current values → Writing → Reload': 1. Check current values : Makes sure the game's values still match what FMAX originally read (If game values changed in the meantime). 2. Writing : Writes your edited values into the game. 3. Reload : Reads the values back from the game to confirm they match what was written. When finished, FMAX shows 'Wrote 3 values to the game · Read back and verified', the updated fields briefly glow green, and an entry like 'Name Crossing 19 → 20' is added to 'Recent edits' in the sidebar. If you use the top Save button across multiple tabs and one tab fails, FMAX notifies you ('1 tab could not be saved · Pending edits remain on Name') and leaves the failed tab's edits waiting in place. When the Save button is disabled Button label Meaning Apply once connected This tab's values weren't read from the currently running game, or the game disconnected afterwards. Once connected, click 'Reload from game' on the tab. Your pending edits stay intact. No game Not connected to the game. Save (dimmed) FMAX is currently reading from or writing to the game. Wait a moment. One-time backup prompt The first time you save any of the following, FMAX asks once: 'Have you backed up your save?' Click 'Yes, backed up' to proceed, and FMAX won't ask again. - Changing a player's Gender (Changing gender) - Editing a player's Match appearance (Match appearance) - Adding, editing, or removing records inside the game —such as names, Nationality, languages, an individual injury, homegrown status, Competition Registration, contract clauses, or Bans - Nationality & City of birth on the info page (shares the same prompt as ⚡ In-game editor actions) When adding or removing records, FMAX advises saving while the game is paused/idle rather than while the date is advancing. What writes immediately The features below do not wait for 'Save'. As soon as you confirm, they write straight to the game. ⚡ In-game editor actions These are the actions under the ⚡ button in an edit tab or the ⚡ items in the right-click menu. Once confirmed, they take effect in the game right away without advancing the date. FMAX asks once for the first time whether you have backed up your save, and there is no undo in FMAX. See Game editor (⚡) for details. Presets applied to multiple items This covers 'Preset for 3 selected' and 'Preset for 120 results' in lists, 'Apply preset', 'Apply custom edit', '⚡ Quick actions', and '⚡ All club players' in the right-click menu, and 'Apply preset' in club tab tables. 1. A confirmation dialog shows what will change and how many items are affected. Click Apply . 2. FMAX reads the current values from the game ('Reading current values from game'). 3. Only values that actually change are written; items that already have the target value are skipped. 4. A notice such as 'Applied "Preset Name" to 120 · Already matched 3 · Failed 0' appears with a Revert button for 9 seconds. If the preset also contains ⚡ In-game editor actions, FMAX runs them one person at a time after writing the values. Those actions cannot be reverted. Presets in an edit tab Picking a preset from the Presets button in an edit tab's header simply fills those values into the tab so you can review them and press 'Save'. However, if the preset includes ⚡ In-game editor actions or Prevent retirement, that part runs immediately and a notice reminds you that 'N changed values require pressing "Save" to enter the game'. Live tweaks and My manager options While turned on, Live tweaks keep writing to the game for as long as FMAX is running—most run when the Game date advances. Clicking options under 'My manager options' on the Live tweaks screen writes to the game immediately, and those settings remain in the game even after you close FMAX. title: What FMAX remembers per save
summary: Which data FMAX keeps separately for each save—such as Live tweaks, Locks, Bookmarks, and Shortlists—which settings apply across all saves, and how FMAX tells saves apart.
text: A regen (newgen) or agent generated in one save might be a completely different person—or nobody at all—in another save. That's why FMAX stores anything pointing to specific people or clubs separately for each save . When you open a different save in the game, FMAX switches over to that save's data automatically. Stored separately per save Feature What is stored per save Live tweaks Enabled live tweaks and their target lists (growth, aging, youth, Prevent retirement, etc.), plus whether Live tweaks was turned on Locks Locked values, 'Values to lock with the Lock button', and whether Locks was turned on Bookmarks Sidebar Bookmarks list Shortlist Every player and staff shortlist Change gender List of players with Keep men’s team eligibility Match appearance Per-player Match appearance list Stats & Record room Season-end records (recorded when 'Save season-end records' is enabled in Settings) Eri Chat history, club management notes, and history of actions run from cards Korean names Record of names FMAX changed in this save, used to revert them (applies when FMAX is in Korean) 'Recent edits' in the sidebar is not saved—it clears whenever you open another save. Shared across all saves FMAX keeps a single copy of these on your PC, so they stay the same whichever save you open: - Every setting on the Settings screen (currency, wage display, hiding CA/PA, lock check interval, etc.) - Presets - Saved filters - Selected columns, sort order, and active filters on each list - Open tabs and theme - On/off toggles and the initial Check backup confirmation for Change gender and Match appearance, plus the on/off toggle and personal dictionary for Korean names - Initial Check backup confirmation for ⚡ Game editor and record editing In a game with multiple human managers, your chosen 'My manager' is remembered by that manager's unique ID. If you open a save with different managers, FMAX asks you to pick again. How FMAX identifies your save FMAX tells saves apart by the folder and file name of the save currently open in the game. You can check the active save under 'Current save' by clicking the connection indicator in the top right, or right beneath the page title on Live tweaks and Locks where it shows 'Current save: Name'. Situation What FMAX does You start a new game and haven't saved yet Stores everything separately under 'Unsaved new game'. The first time you save, FMAX carries it seamlessly over to the new save name. You load a different save in the game Pauses and saves your current save's Live tweaks and Locks, reloads the lists, and loads the other save's data. You reload the same save Shows 'Save reloaded · Reloading lists' and refreshes your lists and tabs. Everything stored for that save stays intact. You Save Game As under a new name in the game Copies your Live tweaks, Locks, Bookmarks, Shortlist, Keep men’s team eligibility, Match appearance, and season records straight over to the new name without pausing. The old save name keeps its own separate copy too. You open an unfamiliar save whose file is identical to a known save (a copied save file, or a backup FM created before overwriting) Carries over that save's Live tweaks, Locks, Bookmarks, Shortlist, Keep men’s team eligibility, Match appearance, and season records, and shows 'Same file as save ‘Name’'. You open a save FMAX has never seen before Starts with Live tweaks and Locks empty. Whenever the save changes, a notification shows 'Save switched: Name' along with what was turned back on (for example, 'Restored previous state: 3 live tweaks · 5 locks'), or tells you 'Live tweaks and Locks are turned off for this save' or 'First time opening this save—Live tweaks and Locks are empty'. While FM is still loading a save, the new file name becomes visible before the previous save's date clears. FMAX waits until loading finishes before deciding, so it won't mistake loading a save for 'Save Game As'. When you restart FMAX If 'Restore previous state when FMAX starts' is enabled in Settings, FMAX turns back on whichever Live tweaks, Locks, Keep men’s team eligibility, and Match appearance settings were active when you closed FMAX. 1. Right on launch, FMAX loads the data from your last opened save without applying it to the game yet. Under the title on Live tweaks and Locks, it shows 'Last opened save: Name · Switches to another save's data if you open a different save in the game'. 2. Once FMAX confirms which save the game has open, it turns back on only what belongs to that save and shows 'Restored previous state'. 3. If the game doesn't report the save name, FMAX keeps using the loaded data as is and shows 'Couldn’t read save name from game … keeping as is' under the title. Turn this setting off if you prefer everything to start paused—you can turn features back on manually on each screen. If you have players set to Keep men’s team eligibility and loaded your save while FMAX was closed, reload the save once after opening FMAX. The game builds its squad registration lists at the moment a save loads. Data from before per-save storage If you had Live tweaks, Locks, Bookmarks, or other data saved from before FMAX stored data per save, FMAX asks once the first time you open a save that has nothing stored yet: - Title: 'Assign your previously saved data to ‘Name’?' - Assign to this save : Makes that data belong to this save and doesn't ask again. - No : Starts this save empty and asks again the next time you open another new save. Nothing from that earlier data is applied to the game until you answer.

Anywhere Key What it does Ctrl+K Opens or closes Quick open. Search by name or Unique ID to open an item in a tab. Tabs and Quick open Ctrl+S Saves unsaved edits across all open tabs to the game at once. When edits are written to the game Ctrl+G Opens the player, staff member, club, or team you're currently viewing in-game in a tab. Ctrl+J Opens or closes the Eri chat panel. Ctrl+Shift+T Reopens the last closed tab along with any unsaved values it had. Press repeatedly to bring back earlier closed tabs. Ctrl+Tab Moves to the next tab. The list screen counts as one stop. Ctrl+Shift+Tab Moves to the previous tab. Ctrl+1 Switches to the list screen. Ctrl+2 ~ Ctrl+8 Jumps to the first through seventh tab from the left. Ctrl+9 Jumps to the last tab. An open menu (right-click menu, Columns, Saved filters, ⚡ menu, etc.) 3. Quick open 4. The Connection status popover 5. Clears all selected rows in a list or in a Club tab table (when your cursor isn't inside a text box). Floating help tooltips also close with Esc . You can also open one from Quick Open ( Ctrl+K ), any underlined player name in another tab, or the squad table in a club tab. See Tabs and Quick Open for more on working with tabs. Change a value and the save bar appears along the bottom. - Each row is one field. Dimmed rows are read-only. - Click a row (or press Enter ) to open its editor. - Numbers: adjust with the − / + buttons, direct typing, ↑ ↓ , or the mouse wheel. Hold Shift while clicking −/+ to step by 5 on 1-point fields like attributes, or by 10× on large numbers. Money fields step in clean round units of your chosen currency. - Dates open a calendar, choice fields open a dropdown list, and colours open a colour picker. - Yes/No fields open as a number input: 1 is Yes and 0 is No. - Press Enter or click elsewhere to keep the value, or press Esc to put back what was there when you opened the row. title: Game editor (⚡)
summary: The ⚡ button at the top of edit tabs runs FM's built-in editor actions—transfers and loans, clearing injuries and unhappiness, terminating contracts, adding homegrown status, and more—straight from FMAX. Choosing a club (transfers, loans, and moves)
Staff transfers: choosing a job and terms
Add to national team (Staff) and Move to another national team (My manager)

Applying to multiple people at once
text: Clicking the ⚡ button on the Player tab. Any upcoming transfer for the player appears at the top, followed by groups such as 'Transfer', 'Status', and 'Record'. What are in-game editor actions? FM27 has its own In-Game Editor (a paid add-on). FMAX's ⚡ menu does the same jobs, but instead of going through the In-Game Editor, it runs the game's own routines directly—so you can use it even if you haven't bought the In-Game Editor. - Changes apply right away. As soon as you click 'Apply now' in the confirmation prompt, the game updates on the spot. You don't need to advance the date or click 'Save'. - They cannot be undone. FMAX has no 'Revert' for these actions. Where an opposite action exists (Freeze attributes ↔ Unfreeze attributes, Grant work permit ↔ Remove work permit, and so on), simply run the opposite action instead. - No In-Game Editor usage is recorded. Because FMAX doesn't go through the In-Game Editor, your save isn't marked as having used it. - Use them while the game is stopped. As the first-time confirmation prompt notes, run these actions when the game is paused on a screen rather than while days are advancing. Every action in the ⚡ menu writes straight to the game as soon as you confirm it. It doesn't wait for 'Save' on the edit tab. These actions cannot be undone. Save a separate backup of your save file before using them for the first time. Where to find it - The ⚡ button at the top right of an edit tab (labelled 'In-game editor actions'). It appears only on the Player, Staff, Team, Club, and My manager tabs—not on other tabs such as Competition, Nation, or City. - Right-click menus in lists also include a group starting with '⚡'. Right-clicking a single person opens their tab and runs the action just as if you picked it from the ⚡ menu. Selecting multiple people and right-clicking shows the '⚡ Quick actions' group (Applying to multiple people at once). For the full right-click menu, see Tabs, quick open, and right-click menus. - To open the My manager tab, click your manager's name under 'My manager & club' on the left. The ⚡ button is available only while FMAX is connected to the game and after the tab has read its data from the game. If FMAX isn't connected or is busy writing something else, it shows 'Not available right now'. How to use it 1. Open a Player, Staff, Team, Club, or My manager tab. 2. Click the ⚡ button and choose an action from the menu. 3. If the action needs extra details (such as a destination club, homegrown club, or morale level), pick them in the next menu or terms window. 4. When you use it for the first time, FMAX asks 'Have you backed up your save?' Click 'Yes, backed up' and it won't ask again. 5. Every action shows a confirmation prompt titled 'Name · Action', explaining what will change and reminding you that it cannot be undone. Click 'Apply now' to run it, or cancel to leave everything untouched. 6. When done, a '…: Applied to game' notice appears and the tab redraws with the updated values. The action is also logged under 'Recent edits' on the left as 'Game editor · '. For major actions—such as transfers, terminating a contract, or national team changes—the confirm button is red. 'Upcoming transfer' and 'Set to retire' under the name On the Player, Staff, and My manager tabs, any scheduled future events in the game appear below the person's name (only when present). - Upcoming transfer · Club · Date · Transfer fee : An agreed future move. Moves agreed on a free at the end of a contract show 'No fee'. This same line also appears at the top of the ⚡ menu. - Set to retire · Date : The retirement date set by the game (for players and staff). Opens the transfer terms window Transfer Move to another club Moves them straight to the chosen club's first team. Choose from 9 rules Record Count as EU player Adds citizenship of an EU, EEA, or EFTA nation so they count as a European player.
