title: Eri
summary: Eri is FMAX's built-in AI chief analyst—reading live game data, leading with clear conclusions backed by numbers, and bringing up action cards when you ask for changes. Connect directly with your Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, or Grok subscription, an API key, or an OpenAI-compatible server (OpenRouter or local models).
text: The Eri screen under Tools on the left—chat in the center, connection and settings on the right. Where to find Eri Eri shows the same conversation in two places: - Right panel: Click the Eri button at the top right of the window or press Ctrl+J to open the side panel from any screen. Click or press it again to close. - Eri screen: Click 'Eri' under Tools on the left for a full chat view with connection, tone, desktop pet, and club policy note settings on the right. You can also jump here using the 'Full view and settings' button in the panel header. Chat history is kept separately for each save. Opening a different save in FM switches to that save's chat, and switching AI connections continues the same conversation. The Eri panel opened from a list screen with Ctrl+J . Connecting for the first time Eri is turned off until you set up a connection. FMAX has no servers of its own—your questions go straight to the AI provider you choose. 1. Open 'Eri' under Tools on the left. 2. Read the notice on the 'Connection' card on the right and click Got it . It explains that game data relevant to your questions will be sent to the AI provider you pick. 3. Choose one of the eight options below. 4. For a subscription connection, click Install and connect (or Sign in if already installed) and sign in with your subscription account in the window and browser that open (Connecting with a subscription). For an API key connection, paste your key into the 'API key' field and click Save . 5. Pick a Model and Reasoning level if needed. Connection Subtitle Cost Claude subscription Claude Code No extra cost (counts toward your plan limit) ChatGPT subscription Codex CLI No extra cost (counts toward your plan limit) Gemini subscription Antigravity CLI No extra cost (counts toward your plan limit) Grok subscription Grok Build No extra cost (counts toward your plan limit) Anthropic API key Claude models Pay-as-you-go billed by the provider OpenAI API key GPT models Pay-as-you-go billed by the provider Google API key Gemini models Pay-as-you-go billed by the provider Custom API OpenAI-compatible API · OpenRouter, local models Charged by that service (free for local models) Subscriptions run on the monthly plan you already pay for; if you hit a usage limit, you simply wait until the provider resets it. API keys draw from your prepaid credit balance with that provider as you go, and each reply shows its cost. Connecting with a subscription With a Subscription connection, FMAX runs Claude Code, Codex CLI, Antigravity CLI, or Grok Build installed on your PC once per question to get a reply. You sign in directly inside that tool—FMAX never touches your login credentials. Usage counts toward your subscription limit, and if you reach the cap, FMAX displays the provider's message as-is. 'Claude subscription' uses a separate tool called Claude Code rather than the regular Claude desktop app. Simply leaving the Claude app open won't connect it, and a Pro plan or higher is required. Each connection shows its current status on the right: 'Checking', 'Not installed', 'Not logged in', 'Logged in', or 'Installed'. One-click install and sign-in: When the subscription you pick shows 'Not installed', you'll see Install and connect ; when it shows 'Not logged in', you'll see Sign in . 1. Clicking the button opens a terminal window (PowerShell). If the tool isn't on your PC yet, FMAX installs it first using the provider's official install command. 2. Next, the sign-in flow starts and your browser opens. Sign in with your subscription account or confirm access. For Gemini (Antigravity), once an input prompt appears after signing in, type /quit or close the window. 3. Meanwhile, the button changes to 'Waiting for sign-in'. FMAX checks every few seconds and automatically switches to that connection with a "Connected" notice once you're signed in (waiting up to 15 minutes). If you don't see the window, check your taskbar. If you installed or signed in manually on your own, click Recheck sign-in status . Update to latest: If the installed tool is out of date, it may lack options FMAX relies on and fail to reply, showing an outdated-version message in chat. Click Update to latest on the Connection card to re-run the provider's official installer; FMAX will let you know when it finishes. ChatGPT subscription: Even if you haven't installed Codex CLI via npm, FMAX will use the bundled Codex inside ChatGPT's Codex desktop app if you have it installed. The model list only shows models your ChatGPT account and installed Codex version can actually use (varying by plan and version). If a previously chosen model is no longer in the list, FMAX falls back to 'Codex default model'. If you still see a message that the model isn't available on your account, pick a different model or click Update to latest . When no reply comes back: If the tool is waiting for a browser sign-in, Eri lets you know and stops. It also stops if there is no response for 4 minutes. Run that tool directly once on your own to finish signing in and any first-run prompts, then ask again. Picking Gemini subscription for the first time brings up a confirmation dialog. Google's terms prohibit third-party apps from using Gemini subscription sign-ins, and accounts have been suspended for doing so. Only click I understand, connect if you accept that risk. Connecting with a Google API key does not have this issue. Gemini subscription connections cannot attach to FMAX tools. Instead, FMAX pre-reads data for your open screen and any players or clubs you mention with @ and bundles it into your question. FMAX tools such as Search criteria, league standings, Fixtures, and Action cards are unavailable, and you cannot attach images. Grok subscription connections do use FMAX tools, though images cannot be sent. When FMAX runs Grok Build, it blocks access to local files and shell commands on your PC so it can only use FMAX tools. Connecting with an API key - API key: Stored exclusively in Windows Cr

title: Shortlist
summary: Collect players and staff into named shortlists. Each save keeps its own shortlists, and you can export or load FM shortlist files (.fmf).
text: The "Shortlist" screen under Tools. Switch or manage shortlists in the top bar, and work with the table below just like the Player list. What shortlists do You can keep as many named shortlists inside FMAX as you like. - Player and Staff shortlists are separate. Switch between them with Player and Staff on the left of the top bar. - Saved separately per save. Loading a different save in FM switches to that save's shortlists. Using "Save Game As" carries your shortlists over to the new save file (What each save remembers separately). - Shortlists live inside FMAX and don't modify game memory. To view a shortlist inside FM, export it as an .fmf file. Screen overview Controls in the top bar: Button What it does Player / Staff Switches between Player shortlists and Staff shortlists Shortlist selector (current name and count) Opens the list of shortlists for the Current save, where you can switch lists, Rename , or Delete this list New list Enter a name and click Create to make an empty shortlist and open it right away Load Picks an .fmf file from FM's shortlists folder and brings it in as an FMAX shortlist Export Writes the current shortlist to FM's shortlists folder as an .fmf file The table below works just like the Player list—column picker, filters, sorting, search, checkboxes, select all, and the right-click menu all work the same way. Columns and filters are remembered separately from the main Player list. If you create a shortlist with the same name as an existing one, FMAX adds a number like "(2)" at the end. Shortlist names can be up to 60 characters long. Adding people to a shortlist You can add people from almost anywhere, and duplicates are skipped automatically: - From a list: Check rows in the Player or Staff list, click Add to shortlist in the bottom bar, and pick a shortlist. - Right-click: Right-click a list row, search result, table row inside a tab, or name link and choose Add to shortlist . If multiple rows are selected, right-clicking one adds everyone selected. - From a Club tab: Check rows in the squad or staff table to bring up the bottom bar, then click Add to shortlist . - From Eri: Click Add n candidates to shortlist on one of Eri's candidate cards, or run a Shortlist card suggested by Eri (Eri). At the bottom of the shortlist picker menu, click Add to new list to name a brand-new shortlist and add them straight to it. A confirmation shows how many people were added to ‘Shortlist name’. Right-clicking a row in a list shows "Add to shortlist" in the context menu. Removing people from a shortlist 1. On the Shortlist screen, check the people you want to remove. 2. Click Remove from list in the bottom bar, or right-click a row and choose Remove from this list . They're removed right away without a confirmation prompt. To put someone back, add them again using any of the methods above. Renaming and deleting a shortlist Click the shortlist name dropdown in the top bar to find Rename and Delete this list at the bottom of the menu. Delete this list permanently removes the FMAX shortlist once confirmed—there is no undo button. Any .fmf files you've already exported to your FM folder are left untouched. Sharing with the game FM stores shortlist files in Documents\Sports Interactive\Football Manager 27\shortlists . FMAX reads and writes .fmf files directly in this folder. Exporting 1. Select the shortlist you want to export and click Export . 2. A notice confirms that ‘Shortlist name.fmf’ was exported with its headcount. Any characters not allowed in file names are replaced with _ . 3. In FM, open the Shortlist screen and click the gear icon → Load Shortlist to load the file. If a file with the same name already exists in the folder, FMAX asks first—click Overwrite to replace it with your current shortlist. Loading 1. Click Load to see the .fmf files in your FM shortlists folder, along with whether each file is for Players or Staff and how many people it contains. 2. Pick a file to create and open a new FMAX shortlist with the same name. You can load both shortlists saved from FM's gear menu and shortlists exported by FMAX. If the file list is empty, save your shortlist from FM's Shortlist gear menu first. Files marked "Can’t read this file" can't be selected. Clicking "Load" lists the shortlist files found in FM's folder. If a loaded shortlist includes people who don't exist in your current save, FMAX lets you know how many out of the total were found in this game—this commonly happens with shortlists made in a different save. Bookmark icon in other lists In the Player and Staff lists, as well as squad and staff tables inside Club tabs, a small bookmark icon appears next to anyone on a shortlist. Hover over it to see which shortlist(s) they belong to. Inside the Shortlist screen itself, the icon is hidden since everyone listed is already on that shortlist. When the list is empty Message on screen What to do No Player (or Staff) shortlists yet Create one with New list or bring one in from FM with Load Nobody is on ‘Shortlist name’ yet Select people from a list and click Add to shortlist No matches found Change your search text or filters Couldn’t find n people from this list in the current game The shortlist may come from a different save

title: Presets
summary: A preset bundles edits together—such as setting specific values—so you can reuse them anytime. Fill a single edit tab with one, or apply it straight to multiple people or your entire filtered results. Presets are saved in FMAX and work in any save.
heads: Two ways to apply: a single tab or multiple targets
Game editor actions and Prevent retirement
text: The Presets screen. Preset lists by type on the left, and the selected preset's details on the right. What is a preset? Each preset has one target type (such as Player, Staff, or Club) and one or more actions . An action tells FMAX what to do to a single field or a group of fields—for example, setting all Technical attributes to 20 or adding 5 to CA. - Presets are saved in FMAX itself, so you can use them in any save. - You can export and import them as JSON files to share with other players. - Click Presets under Tools in the left sidebar to open this screen. Two ways to apply: a single tab or multiple targets When a preset writes to the game depends on where you apply it. Where you apply it When it writes to the game Undo A single edit tab Only updates the values shown in the tab. Click 'Save' to write them to the game Nothing is written to the game until you click 'Save' Multiple people (lists, right-click menu, club squad tables) Writes straight to the game as soon as you click 'Apply' in the confirmation dialog Click 'Revert' on the notice to undo once Applying in an edit tab Clicking the Presets button in a player tab. Presets are grouped by category, with a short summary under each name. 1. Click Presets (the icon with two horizontal bars) in the top-right corner of the edit tab. 2. Pick a preset from the menu. Only presets matching this tab's type appear, grouped by category. 3. The values in the tab update so you can check what changed. 4. Click 'Save' to write them to the game. A preset applied in a tab is not written to the game until you click 'Save'. A notice also reminds you: 'Changed N values with "Name". Click "Save" to apply to the game.' You can only apply a preset once the tab has finished reading from the game. If nothing would change, FMAX shows 'No values changed with "Name"'. At the bottom of the menu are two more buttons: - Create preset from current values : Opens a new preset in the Presets screen pre-filled with the values currently shown in this tab (including unsaved edits). Numeric fields such as attributes, personality, and positions are included, while money amounts, reputation, fitness, contract details, Overview, ability (CA & PA), appearance, and Player traits are left out. Its name defaults to 'Values of …' and its category to 'Templates'. Remove any rows you don't need and click 'Save' to keep it as a preset. - Manage presets : Opens the Presets screen. If a preset contains 'In-game editor actions' or 'Add to prevent-retirement list', those actions run immediately after a confirmation prompt even when applied from a tab. Field values still wait for 'Save'. Applying to multiple people You can apply a preset to multiple people from several places: - After selecting multiple rows in a list , click 'Preset for N selected' in the bottom bar. - After narrowing a list with filters or search (with nobody selected), click 'Preset for N results' in the bottom bar to apply it to every matching result. - Right-click in a list → under 'Edit', choose 'Apply preset' or 'Apply custom edit' . Works on a single person or a multi-selection. - Above the squad or staff table in a club tab , click 'Presets' to apply it to everyone in that table (Club). The steps are the same whichever route you take: 1. The menu header reads 'Apply preset to … · Writes to game'. Pick a preset. 2. An 'Apply "Name" to N people' confirmation dialog appears, showing what the preset will do and noting that changes are written to the game immediately. 3. Click 'Apply'. FMAX reads the current values from the game, calculates the new ones, and writes them back, showing 'Writing to game N / All' as it progresses. 4. When finished, an 'Applied "Name" to N people' notice appears along with counts for anyone whose values already matched, failed, or could not be found in the game. Applying a preset to multiple people writes straight to the game without clicking 'Save'. Revert: The notice includes a 'Revert' button for about 9 seconds. Click it to restore the values changed in this batch to what they were beforehand, followed by a 'Reverted "Name" N / All' notice. You can only undo the single most recent bulk apply, and any values changed in the meantime by the game or another edit are left untouched. 'Revert' only restores field values. In-game editor actions included in a preset cannot be undone. Any open tabs for those people automatically reload with the new values. If you apply a preset to a locked field, the lock updates to the new value too (Locks). Apply custom edit Build and run a one-off edit without saving a preset first. 1. Click 'Apply custom edit' at the bottom of the bulk preset menu (or from the right-click menu). 2. The Presets screen opens with a banner at the top: 'Choose actions to apply to …'. 3. Use 'Add action' to set up the edits you want. 4. Click 'Apply' in the banner to confirm and write straight to the game—you don't need to save it first. Click 'Save' if you also want to keep it as a preset. 5. Click 'Cancel' in the banner to back out. If you open a different save in the game after selecting your targets, FMAX stops and shows 'Save changed—nothing was applied'. Select your targets again in the current save. Built-in presets Presets included with FMAX out of the box, marked Built-in in the list. Target Name What it does Player Legend: all outfield attributes 20 Sets all Technical, Mental, Physical, and Set Pieces attributes to 20 (Goalkeeping attributes stay as is) Player World-class: outfield attributes at least 17 Raises only values below 17 in those same groups up to 17 Player Outfield attributes +1 Adds 1 to every attribute in those groups Player Outfield attributes −1 Subtracts 1 from every attribute in those groups Player All goalkeeping attributes 20 Sets all Goalkeeping attributes to 20 Player Best hidden attributes Consistency, Important Matches, and Versatility to 20; Dirtiness and Injury Proneness to 1 Player Both feet 20 Left Foot and Right Foot to 20 Player CA &

title: Locks
summary: Locked values stay put while FMAX is running—whenever the game changes them, FMAX writes them back. Lock individual values with the padlock icon, or lock a preselected set all at once with the 'Lock' button.
heads: Locking a single value: the padlock
Locking multiple values at once: the 'Lock' button
The 'Locks N' indicator in the top bar
text: The Locks screen. On the left are the values to lock with the 'Lock' button; on the right are the values currently locked. How Locks work While FMAX is running, it checks your locked values against the game at a set interval (1 second by default). Whenever the game changes a locked value, FMAX writes the locked value back. - Checks run regardless of the game date —Locks keep working even while the game is paused or idle. - Values are protected only while FMAX is running . Once you quit FMAX, the game can change them freely. - Unlocking a field leaves the game value at whatever it is at that moment. - Locks are remembered separately for each save (What FMAX remembers per save). 'Current save: …' at the top of the screen shows which save the current list belongs to. Locks write directly to the game. You don't need to press 'Save'—any change the game makes is reverted right away. Locking a single value: the padlock 1. In an edit tab, hover over a value row to reveal a padlock icon next to the number (tooltip: 'Lock this value'). 2. Click the padlock to lock it at the value currently read from the game . The icon switches to a closed padlock. 3. Click it again to unlock it. Once locked, a field's padlock stays visible in the accent color even when your cursor isn't over the row. - Only numeric values have padlocks; fields that cannot be locked don't show one. - Before a tab has read data from the game, FMAX lets you know that you can lock values once they have been read from the game. - If you edit a field and click its padlock before saving, FMAX locks the current game value first; once you press 'Save', the locked value updates to your new value. - If you edit and save a locked value in a tab, or change it with a preset or the Game editor, the locked value automatically updates to follow the new value. Locking your first value turns Locks on automatically. Locking multiple values at once: the 'Lock' button The Lock button (padlock icon) at the top right of an edit tab locks all the fields configured under 'Values for the Lock button' on the Locks screen at their current game values in one go. Click it again to unlock those fields. When every configured field is locked, the button lights up. If you haven't chosen any fields yet, FMAX shows a notice asking you to pick values first along with an 'Open lock settings' button. Locking multiple people - Select multiple rows in a list and 'Lock selected' appears in the bottom bar. - 'Lock values' in the right-click menu (or 'Lock values for N' with multiple items selected) does the same thing. Clicking either opens a 'Lock N' confirmation prompt listing the N configured fields to lock at their current game values. Confirming reads the values from the game and locks them. Both buttons only appear when at least one field is configured on the Locks screen. The Locks screen Click Locks in the left tools list or 'Locks N' in the top bar of the window to open the Locks screen. Status bar and buttons Status Meaning No locked values Nothing is currently locked Active — keeping game values locked Running normally Paused — game values aren’t being kept You clicked 'Pause all'. Your list is still kept Waiting for game (…) Not connected to the game, or a save is loading On the right of the status bar, 'Rewritten N times · Checking every Ns' shows how many times FMAX has reverted changes made by the game so far. - Pause all / Resume : Pauses or resumes enforcement while keeping your list of locked values intact. - Unlock all : Empties the entire list after a confirmation prompt ('Unlock all N locked values? Current game values will stay as they are.'). Values for the Lock button Pick a type (Player, Staff, Club, etc.) at the top right to choose which fields the 'Lock' button and 'Lock selected' will lock for that type. 1. Click 'Add value' and pick a field, or click 'All in group' next to a group heading to add every field in that group. 2. Choose a mode for each row: - Keep exact value : Reverts the value whether the game raises or lowers it. - Allow increases : Lets the game raise the value and only blocks drops. Whenever the value goes up, the locked value moves up to match it. 3. Click the trash button to remove a row. For players, Injury Proneness and Dirtiness are included by default—feel free to change them. Currently locked Active locks are listed grouped by person or club. - Open next to a name: Opens that item's tab. - Unlock all : Unlocks every field on that person or club. - Value chips: Shown as 'Field name value', with '↑ allowed' added when set to 'Allow increases'. Click × on a chip to unlock just that field. Items not found in game If FMAX can't find a locked person or club in the game, 'Not found in game' appears next to them in the 'Currently locked' list, the status bar notes 'N not found', and the 'Locks N' badge at the top of the window switches to a warning color. This can happen if you loaded a different save or the item no longer exists in the game. FMAX keeps checking for missing items and resumes protecting them automatically if they reappear. If you no longer need them, remove them with 'Unlock all'. Check interval Under 'Lock check interval' in Settings, choose 0.5s, 1s, 2s, or 5s. Shorter intervals revert changes faster whenever the game modifies a value. The 'Locks N' indicator in the top bar Whenever at least one value is locked, a padlock and 'Locks N' (or 'Locks N · Stopped' when paused) appear at the top of the window. Hover to check the current status, or click to open the Locks screen. A count also appears next to 'Locks' in the left tools list. When you reopen FMAX When 'Restore previous state on startup' is enabled in Settings (the default), Locks that were active when you closed FMAX turn back on automatically—once FMAX checks which save is open in FM27, it activates only the locks belonging to that save. If you turn that setting off, Locks start paused instead. Faster growth and Slower aging in Live tweaks leave locked

title: Compare
summary: Place two open tabs of the same type (two players, two clubs, and so on) side by side to see how their values differ. Compare is strictly read-only and writes nothing to the game.
text: Comparing two players—pickers for both players at the top, player cards underneath, and grouped values with their differences below. How to open Compare Compare works across already open tabs , so you need at least two tabs of the same type open first. 1. From a list, open the two players (or two clubs, etc.) you want to compare in tabs. 2. Click the Compare button (shaped like two squares) near the top right of either tab. 3. The Compare screen opens with the tab you clicked on the left and the other tab of the same type on the right. You can also open Compare from Tools in the left sidebar. If you don't have two tabs of the same type open yet, you'll see 'Open two tabs of the same type'. Clicking the Compare button on a tab when no second tab of that type is open prompts you to open one more tab of that type to compare. Compare is strictly for viewing. You can't edit values here, and nothing is ever written to the game. Screen layout Top bar - Type picker (top right): When you have pairs of tabs open for more than one type (for example, two players and two clubs), pick which type to compare. - Differences only : Hides rows where both sides match so only differing values remain on screen. - Left & right pickers : Click either name field to switch to another open tab of the same type. Whichever tab is chosen on one side is hidden from the other side's dropdown. - View tab : Jumps straight to that person's or item's tab. - Center ⇄ button : Swaps the Left and right sides. - Far right: Shows the count of differing values or 'All values match'. Player cards When comparing players, both player cards appear near the top. Because player cards are drawn from live in-game values, edits you've made on a tab without saving won't show up on the cards. For what each part of the card means, see Stats, player cards, and Record room. Value tables Fields are organized into the same groups used on edit tabs (Technical, Mental, Goalkeeping, Personality, and so on). At the very top, the Summary group shows calculated readouts such as age, Primary position, Recommended Current Ability, and Attribute effectiveness. Column Meaning Field Field name as shown on the edit tab Left Value from the Left tab Right Value from the right tab Diff Right value minus Left value . Shown only when numeric values differ—rates in percentage points (%p), and money in your chosen currency Rows where the two sides differ are highlighted. Dropdown choices, dates, and text fields display both values side by side without calculating a diff. List-based sections (such as relationships and languages) are not shown in Compare. Unsaved edits The value tables in Compare read what is currently shown on each tab —including edits you've typed into a tab without clicking 'Save' yet. That lets you tweak attributes on a tab and immediately check how the player stacks up against someone else. When you're ready to write those edits into FM, head back to that tab and click 'Save' (When edits are written to the game).

title: Stats, Player Cards & Record room
summary: Covers the Stats page in player tabs, FMAX player cards and PNG exports, Club records in club tabs, and league-wide rankings in the Record room. Everything on these screens only reads from the game.
text: Every screen covered on this page only reads from the game—nothing here edits your save. The only exceptions are choosing a custom photo on a player card and turning on 'Use in game'. Player Stats page Click Stats on the left side of a player tab. At the top are three tabs: Season details , League rankings , and Overview . Whichever tab you viewed last opens automatically for the next player too. Stats › Season details. This season’s stats broken down by competition. Season details Shows This season’s stats in columns by competition. Columns only appear for competitions the player has played in. Column Meaning All competitions Combined total across League, Cup, Continental, and International matches League / Cup / Continental / International / Friendly Stats from that competition type Overall club Separate club total tracked by the game - Total / Per 90: Pick Per 90 to divide counting stats by the player's Playing time in that competition and show per-90-minute rates. Percentages, ratings, and Playing time stay as they are. - Rows are grouped into Matches, Scoring, Chance creation, Passing, Defending, Work rate, and Mistakes & discipline. Goalkeepers get an extra Goalkeeping group (goals conceded, clean sheets, and xG prevented). - Career appearances and goals, along with career league appearances and goals, appear in the top right. Career history: Below the table, season-by-season rows mirror the game's history screen. Appearances, goals, assists, Player of the Match awards, and rating show league figures; click a row to expand the competition breakdown for that season. The 'Transfer' column shows how the player joined that club (transfer fee, loan, or Free transfer). Career history is fetched directly from the game's history screen. If FMAX is running in read-only mode or the game is running as administrator, 'Could not load career history' appears instead. Awards: Season awards from the game are listed newest first, including second- and third-place finishes where the game records them. If there are more than 12, click Show all . Team of the Year entries only exist for seasons since the save started. Comparison settings League rankings and Overview compare the player against peers in the same position. Use the top bar to choose the comparison pool—these settings apply across all players. Field Options Competition All competitions, League, Cup, Continental, International, Overall club, Friendly Compare leagues Top 20 leagues, Same league only, All leagues (men’s and women’s pools are separated automatically to match the player) Position Primary position (auto), or Goalkeeper, Centre-back, Full-back, Defensive/central mid, Winger, Attacking mid, Striker Min. minutes No limit, or 450 to 2,700 mins (defaults to 900 mins) Above the table, the active pool is summarized as '… · n players compared'. If a player falls short of Min. minutes or lacks enough recorded stats, no grade is given and FMAX explains why. League rankings Shows the value, Percentile, and rank for every stat. - Value: Counting stats are shown Per 90; percentages stay as percentages and list the number of attempts. - Percentile: The percentage of players in the comparison pool below this player. Ties count as half. - Lower is better: For mistakes, Possession lost, fouls, Yellow & red cards, Offsides, and goals conceded, a higher percentile means fewer committed or conceded. - Last season column: When the game has stats from the same competition last season, the previous value appears beside an arrow—green for improved, red for worse. Click any row to expand a distribution bar across all compared players, the top 1–10, and the ranks right around this player. Click View full rankings → to open the Record room with closely matching filters. Stats › League rankings. Click a row to expand the distribution and rankings. Overview At the top are the player card, a summary strip for this season (appearances, Playing time, goals, assists, Average rating, and xG & xA—or clean sheets & xG prevented for goalkeepers), and card details. Below that, in order: Section Details Season report card A grade and 'Top n% in position'. Grades are based on percentile within the comparison pool: 90+ A+, 80+ A, 65+ B, 45+ C, 25+ D, and below 25 F. Shows the score and weight for each area (scoring, Chance creation, pressing, etc.); click any area to expand its stats and percentiles. Low-sample percentages are pulled toward 50 Percentile profile A radar chart of 6–8 key stats suited to the player's position Two stat panels Distribution and percentiles for Finishing and Chance creation (shot-stopping and build-up for goalkeepers) Compare two stats A scatter plot of compared players. Pick stats for the X-axis and Y-axis , and click Swap axes to flip them. Hover over a dot to preview the player, or click to open their tab. Next to the chart are the 6 Most similar players across those two stats Recent seasons Club, appearances, goals, assists, rating, Ability score, and Report card for this season and the previous 3 seasons Season trends Plots Ability score, Average rating, goals, assists, or xG across seasons as a line chart. A hollow dot marks the current season in progress Positions played A pitch graphic shaded by appearances at each spot, filterable by season and club or International Past seasons' Ability scores and Report cards come from snapshots FMAX saved during those seasons. Save season-end records must be turned on in Settings; any season where FMAX wasn't running shows 'No record'. For seasons before the save started, the game only holds appearances and goals. Stats › Overview. The player card sits in the top left. Player cards Player cards generated by FMAX appear in Stats › Overview, on the Compare screen, in Card view on a club tab's squad table, and in Best Eleven lineups under Club records. - Main number (Ability score): A 1–99 score calculated from Current Ability (CA), RCA (Recommended Current Ability), and Primary position fit, with po

title: Tactics
summary: Reads your team's tactic to show who fits best in every spot and highlight empty or weak spots. You can also edit a tactic and export it as a new tactic file without changing anything live in the game.
heads: See which works best in the Tactic Arena
text: What the Tactics screen does Click Tactics under Tools in the left sidebar to open it. When you open it with a save loaded in FM27, FMAX reads your manager's club tactics and first-team squad and lays everything out on a single screen. - Use it just to check your lineup. It suggests a starter and candidate for every spot, and flags any empty or weak spots. - Edit and experiment. Try out different roles, Player Instructions, Team Instructions, and Mentality right here, then export your version as a new tactic file. - Nothing inside the running game is changed. Your edits only enter the game when you load the exported file on FM27's tactics screen. Even when FM27 isn't running, you can still open saved tactic files. Because FMAX can't read your squad offline, starters and candidates stay blank. Around the screen Choosing a tactic Pick what to view from the Tactic row at the top of the screen. - In-game tactics : Shows buttons for each tactic currently set up on your tactics screen in FM27. The one your team is using right now is marked 'In use'. - Open saved tactic file : Opens files from your game's tactics folder ( Sports Interactive\Football Manager 27\tactics inside your Documents folder). Downloaded tactics placed in that folder show up here too, or you can drag and drop a tactic file (.fmf) straight into the FMAX window without moving it first. Below that, Tactics folder shows which folder FMAX is reading right now, and Choose folder lets you point it somewhere else. Click Reload in the top-right corner to re-read your current tactics and squad from the game—handy right after you tweak your tactic or lineup in FM27. The pitch Your tactic's positions and roles are laid out on the pitch (Attacks toward top). - Use Combined / In Possession / Out of Possession above the pitch to choose which phase's shape and roles to view. Combined shows the In Possession positions with both phases' roles listed together. - Under each spot's role, FMAX shows the name of its suggested starter. - Empty spot : No one in your current first-team squad fits that spot as a starter. - Weak spot : That spot's starter is weaker than your team average. Spot details Click any spot on the pitch to inspect it on the right. Click the spot again or click Clear selection to close the panel. Row Meaning In-game pick The player currently assigned to that spot on the game's tactics screen. Marked 'Differs from suggestion' if it doesn't match FMAX's pick Suggested starter The player in your current first team who FMAX rates as the best fit for this spot Candidate The next-best fit for this spot behind the starter In Possession / Out of Possession The Position, Roles, Duty, and any custom Player Instructions set for each phase Next to each player's name you'll see their ability for this spot, age, condition, Match sharpness, and Role ability. Hover over any unfamiliar term to see what it means, or click a player's name to open their edit tab. When no spot is selected, the right panel shows Spots to fix first (starting with empty or weak spots), Picked in game (how many of your in-game starters differ from FMAX's suggestions), and Left out due to injury. Starters and candidates are chosen by the same rules as Recruitment analysis: among first-team players familiar enough with the position, FMAX picks in order of highest ability for that spot, puts each player in at most one spot, and leaves out injured players. Team Instructions Instructions for the whole team are grouped by phase. Dimmed text means the instruction is still at its default setting. Editing a tactic Click Edit tactic in the top-right corner to enter edit mode. A bar at the top shows 'Editing' along with how many changes you've made. - Name and Mentality : Change these above the pitch. - Position, Roles, Duty, and Player Instructions : Click a spot on the pitch and pick them on the right. You set In Possession and Out of Possession separately. Instructions marked 'Locked by role' are built into that role and can't be changed. - Team Instructions : Pick these in the Team Instructions area below the pitch. Button What it does Revert changes Discards every edit made here and goes back to the original tactic Done editing Closes edit mode. Your edits stay in memory so you can reopen edit mode and keep working Export to file Saves your edited tactic to the game's tactics folder as a new file , leaving the original tactic and file untouched After exporting, head to the tactics screen in FM27 and load the new file to use it. Nothing changes in your live game while you edit here. Load the exported file inside FM27 to put it into play. Good to know: - The goalkeeper spot can't be moved, and you can't drag a spot onto one that's already occupied. - Roles and Player Instructions that FM27 doesn't allow for that position and formation can't be selected. - Files saved in an older game format are view-only and can't be edited. Load the tactic in FM27 and save it again first. - You can't export if your game's tactics folder has no saved tactic files in it at all. Save any tactic once inside FM27 first. See which works best in the Tactic Arena Located at the bottom of edit mode, this tool creates variants of your current tactic that change just one thing and adds them to the Tactic Arena test queue. Because the Arena runs every variant under identical conditions, you can see cleanly how much that one tweak moves your points. 1. title: Tactic Arena
summary: Have the game play out hundreds of matches with your tactic files and rank them by points to see which ones come out on top. It works in three steps: create a test sheet, run your tactics, and read the rankings.
heads: Using the same conditions as the Official test
Sending tactics over from the Tactics screen
text: What is the Tactic Arena? Click Tactic Arena under Tools in the left sidebar to open it. It has the game play hundreds of matches on your behalf using your tactic files, then ranks your tactics based on the results. There are five tabs across the top. Tab What it does Table View the rankings so far for each test sheet Run tests Pick the tactic files you want to compare and run matches Auto search Have FMAX tweak instructions one at a time on a single tactic to find a stronger setup Test sheet Choose the test team and its opponents Official test A standardized test every user runs under the same conditions, covered separately in Official test and the Tactic Lab How to use in the top right walks you through the three steps from setup to reading the rankings. You can't play the game while a test is running—leave the game paused and don't advance the date. In Live tweaks, Lock AI manager tactics and 100% tactical effectiveness are paused while testing runs and turned back on once it finishes. Getting started: three steps 1. Create a test sheet. Pick a test team and its opponents. Once you make one, you can keep reusing it. 2. Run your tactics. Pick the tactic files you want to compare and click Start. The game plays out the matches for you. 3. Read the rankings. Higher expected points mean a stronger tactic. If two tactics' ranges overlap, it's still too close to call. FMAX reads tactic files from your game's tactics folder ( Sports Interactive\Football Manager 27\tactics inside your Documents folder). Any tactic you save on the tactics screen in FM shows up here. Every tactic picker includes a Tactics folder line showing which folder FMAX is currently reading. If your tactics aren't listed, click Choose folder there to point FMAX to the folder where your tactics live, or drag and drop a tactic file (.fmf) straight into the FMAX window. For details, see 'Tactic files don't show up in the list' under Troubleshooting. Test sheets A test sheet sets identical match conditions for every candidate you compare. It bundles together one AI team to run the tactic, a set of AI opponent teams, squad and familiarity rules, and baseline set pieces. Set one up once and reuse it anytime—all results run on the same test sheet accumulate in a single rankings table. Field Meaning Test team Not the club you manage yourself. Pick the senior squad of any AI-managed club in your current save (clubs managed by a human can't be chosen). FMAX hands the tactic file under test to this club's AI manager and plays out the matches Opponents Pick between 1 and 40 AI-managed clubs. Each round plays every chosen opponent once at home and once away. You can assign a specific tactic and set piece file to each opponent (if you assign a tactic, you must also assign set pieces), and that opponent will always play with those files. If left blank, it isn't random—that club's AI manager picks tactics and set pieces just as they normally do in the game. Opponents' tactics and set pieces never change, no matter what you compare in Run tests Use equal squads When on, both the test team and all opponents use identical test squads so player ability doesn't skew the comparison (Role squad: 26 standard players tailored to each position / Uniform squad: every outfield player has the exact same attributes). When off, each team plays with its real players Max tactical familiarity When on, both sides play at full tactical familiarity so a new tactic isn't penalized for being unfamiliar. When off, each team plays at its actual familiarity Baseline set pieces Set pieces locked onto the 'Test team' alone when comparing tactics. Opponents don't use these—they use whatever you assigned per opponent above (or their AI manager's choice). You must set baseline set pieces to use Tactic comparison and Auto search Name Leave blank to name it automatically after the team and number of opponents There are two kinds of test sheets: - Standard test : Every opponent's tactic and set pieces are locked to files, and both Use equal squads and Max tactical familiarity are turned on. Because the test is identical regardless of who runs it or in which save, you can share and merge rankings files with other FMAX users on the same game version. - My save test : Any test sheet missing at least one of those three conditions (AI managers pick opponent tactics, teams use real players, or teams use actual familiarity). Results can only be compared within your current save and can't be merged with other users' rankings. At the bottom of the test sheet builder, FMAX shows which type your sheet qualifies as and what else you need to fill in to make it a Standard test. Its name starts with 'Official conditions practice'. To submit an official score, test in the Official test tab. - If an official club isn't available in your save, FMAX substitutes a replacement club just like Official test does. - If the Tactic Lab later updates its official test sheet, your sheet gets marked 'Official test sheet changed'. Click Create again to build one with the current conditions. Test sheets marked 'Legacy' are records from an older version of FMAX. You can view them, but you can't run more matches on them—create a new test sheet to test again. Run tests 1. Choose a test sheet. Pick which test sheet to run on. 2. What to compare. Whatever you pick here, opponents always keep the tactics and set pieces defined on the test sheet—only the 'Test team' changes. - Tactic comparison : Swaps only the tactic on the 'Test team' one candidate at

title: Official test and Tactic Lab
summary: An Official test runs every FMAX user's tactic with the exact same club, squad, and opponents. Run it from the 'Official test' tab in the Tactic Arena to save results to your Tactic Lab account and upload your tactic.
heads: What gets recorded and uploaded to Tactic Lab
text: What is the Official test? You'll find it in Official test , the fifth tab of the Tactic Arena. Tests you run with your own test sheet use whichever teams and opponents you picked, so it's hard to compare your numbers directly with someone else's. An Official test puts every FMAX user on equal footing— the exact same club, the exact same squad, and the exact same opponents . Because the setup never changes, anyone can test anywhere and compare results side by side. Pick a tactic file and press start: FM27 plays out the matches for you and reports the tactic's Season points (the points you can expect over a 38-match season). Tactic Lab is where all of those results come together. Every Official test you finish is recorded to your Tactic Lab account, and any tactics you upload can be viewed by other players. If you see 'Tactic Lab is not open yet', Official tests aren't available at the moment. In the meantime, you can still compare tactics head-to-head with your own test sheet in the Run tests tab. Before you start Readiness check Opening the tab runs a quick check first. Every row needs to say 'Passed' before you can start. Any row that doesn't pass explains what's wrong and how to fix it—once you've sorted it out, click Check again . Check What it looks for Game connection Whether the game is running with a save loaded Match engine Whether your game version and match engine are supported for Official tests. Match engine mods will fail this check Test clubs Whether the two clubs set on the test sheet are available in the current save. If not, stand-in clubs are used instead The game’s default tactics Whether the game’s default tactics used by opponent clubs are unmodified. Everyone needs the original files so you face the exact same opponents Tactic Lab account Whether an account is linked to record your results Stand-in clubs step in when the official clubs aren't playable in your current save. FMAX matches their squads and club conditions to the official clubs, so the result counts as the exact same test—it simply leaves a note that stand-in clubs were used. Linking your Tactic Lab account 1. On the Tactic Lab account row of the check list, click Link account . Your browser will open. 2. Sign in with Discord in your browser. Make sure the confirmation code shown in your browser matches the confirmation code in FMAX, then confirm the link. 3. Once you're signed in, the row in FMAX automatically updates to 'Linked as …'. - FMAX never sees or receives your Discord password. - Click Unlink to disconnect your account. Results already recorded on Tactic Lab stay there, though you won't be able to run Official tests or upload tactics until you link again. Running a test 1. Choose a tactic to test. Pick from the tactic files in your game's tactics folder—any tactic you've saved on FM27's tactics screen shows up here. If a tactic you just saved isn't listed, click Refresh list . Still missing? Click Choose folder on the Tactics folder row right below to point FMAX to the right folder, or drag and drop a tactic file (.fmf) straight into the FMAX window. 2. Choose how accurately to test. Pick Precise, Standard, or Fast. If it's your first run, Standard is a good place to start. 3. Review the tactic, match count, and estimated time on the card on the right, then click Start official test . FMAX will ask you to confirm once more. Playing more matches narrows the range and gives you a firmer result, at the cost of taking longer. Option Matches When to use Precise 1,000 matches Pinpoint accuracy when separating tactics on the leaderboard Standard (recommended) 400 matches Plenty accurate for most tests Fast 200 matches Quick ballpark check While a test is running, please follow these rules: don't advance the date in-game (don't click Continue), don't save the game or load another save, and don't close FM27 or FMAX. If the game date moves forward or a save is loaded, the test stops on the spot. In Live tweaks, Lock AI manager tactics and 100% tactical effectiveness pause automatically while the test runs and turn back on once it finishes. While a test is running The whole tab switches to a progress view showing the matches left, a progress bar, the tactic, total matches, and the clubs. Click Stop test to pause at any time. All matches played so far are kept, and you can pick up right where you left off from the same save on the same game date. Resuming a stopped test A stopped test stays pinned as a card at the top of the tab, telling you why it stopped and which game date you need in order to resume. - Resume : Click this while the save you started the test in is open on that exact game date. - Start new : Leave the stopped test as it is and start a fresh run with your choice of tactic and match count. Why it stopped What to do Stopped because the game date advanced If you haven't saved, reload the save to return to that date and click Resume. If you've already saved past it, you can't resume—click Start new Stopped because a save was reloaded If it's the same save on the same date, go ahead and click Resume Stopped because a different save was loaded Reload the save you started the test in, then click Resume Stopped because the game stopped responding Once the game is responsive again, click Resume Tests started more than 7 days ago can no longer be resumed, though the matches played up to that point remain in your records. Reading your results When the run finishes, a result card appears. - Season points : The points you can expect over a 38-match season with this tactic. Higher means a stronger tactic. - Range : How much match-to-match luck can sway the score. Your tactic's true points almost certainly sit inside this span. More matches narrow the range; if two tactics' ranges overlap, it's still too close to tell which one is stronger. - Matches played and W-D-L. If you've tested the same tactic more than once, FMAX also shows the combined totals across your past runs. View details in Rankings op

title: Live tweaks
summary: Live tweaks are rules that stay active in the game for as long as FMAX is open. They include Faster growth, Slower aging, Prevent retirement, auto-accepting offers, Prevent AI manager sackings, and Lock AI manager tactics—all remembered separately for each save.
heads: What happens when you turn a tweak off?
Always accept my transfer & loan offers
Block player rejection on accepted transfers
Value my players like AI clubs
text: The Live tweaks screen. The status box at the top shows which live tweaks are currently on, followed by the group tabs and the list of tweaks below. What live tweaks are Live tweaks aren't one-off edits—they are ongoing rules you leave on . - They keep writing to the game while FMAX is open, and stop as soon as you close FMAX. - Most of them act only when the game date advances . While the game is paused on the same day, they do nothing. - You don't need to click 'Save'. Turning a tweak on puts it straight to work. - Click Live tweaks under Tools in the left sidebar to open this screen. Whenever any tweaks are running, a count next to it shows how many are on. Live tweaks write directly to the game without clicking 'Save'. As the notice at the top of the screen advises, save a separate backup of your game before using them. Around the screen Top bar - Current save: Name — Shows which save the current list belongs to (Separate for each save). - Pause all / On — Appears at the top right whenever at least one live tweak is on. 'Pause all' stops writing to the game while leaving your list and switches untouched. Click 'On' to get them running again. Status box The top line tells you what Live tweaks is doing right now. Status Meaning No live tweaks are on You haven't turned any live tweaks on Active. Writes to the game whenever the game date advances Running normally Paused. Nothing is written to the game You clicked 'Pause all' Starts once you load a save The game is running, but no save is loaded yet Starting Turning on Waiting for the game (…) Not connected to the game yet, or still getting ready; the reason is in parentheses Turning off… Check that the game code has been restored You turned off a 'Game code' tweak and FMAX is still restoring the original code Below that, you'll see: - Active tweak names — Click any name to jump straight to its row (switching group tabs automatically if needed). - Your manager options · Active in game — Any My manager options you've enabled appear on their own line here. - Warnings — Lists any tweak that ran into an issue, along with its name and why. Tweaks you turned off whose game code hasn't finished restoring yet also appear here. Group tabs and tweak rows Filter the list using the All · Player · Transfers & contracts · Manager & board · AI manager tabs. The number next to a tab shows how many tweaks in that group are on. FMAX remembers whichever tab you picked for next time. Each live tweak row is laid out like this: - Name , plus a 'Game code' badge on tweaks that patch the game's code. - A one-line summary and 'Details' (click to expand the full explanation). - Status line — What the tweak is currently doing (for example, 'Declines slowed: 0 · Current targets: 389'). Green means everything is working normally; orange indicates a warning. - A switch on the right, or an 'Add rule' , 'Add person' , 'Add team' , or 'Add manager' button. At the very bottom, Recent activity logs up to the last 14 actions taken by your tweaks (Recent activity). Turning tweaks on and off 1. Flip a row's switch on, or add an entry with 'Add rule' (or the row's add button). 2. If Live tweaks was paused, turning on a switch or adding a rule resumes it automatically. 3. The first time you turn on a tweak with a 'Game code' badge, a 'Have you backed up your save?' dialog appears once. It shows how many places in the game code will be modified and notes that turning the tweak off or closing FMAX normally restores the original code. Click 'Yes, backed up' to turn it on—you won't be asked again. 4. To turn a tweak off, flip its switch off or delete its rules with the trash icon. To pause everything at once, click 'Pause all'. Separate for each save Your tweak list and on/off states are remembered separately for each save . - Load a different save in FM, and FMAX switches to that save's live tweaks. One save's tweaks are never written into another save. - If you create a new save file in the game (for example with 'Save Game As'), it starts out inheriting the previous save's live tweaks and tracks them separately from then on. - When you reopen FMAX, any tweaks that were on when you closed it turn back on automatically if 'Restore previous state on startup' is enabled in Settings (on by default). FMAX checks which save is open in the game first and turns on only that save's tweaks. - If FMAX hasn't identified the save yet, the top of the screen shows 'Last opened save: … · Switches automatically if you load a different save in game'. The 'Yes, backed up' confirmation is asked only once across all saves. See What FMAX remembers per save for the full picture. What happens when you turn a tweak off? What stays and what reverts after turning a tweak off depends on how that tweak works. Type Live tweaks When turned off Patches game code ('Game code' badge) The three auto-accept offer tweaks, Value my players like AI clubs, Max 1-on-1 talk score, Max tactical effectiveness, Lock AI manager tactics, Prevent AI manager sackings, Lift age limits too Turning it off, clicking Pause all, or closing FMAX restores the original game code. Anything that already happened while it was on (completed transfers and contracts, player values recalculated and saved by the game, match records already played) remains Keeps a game setting on Approve all board requests, Max extra staff slots, Golden Generation, Show everyone in search Turning it off or clicking Pause all reverts only what FMAX turned on (or the extra slots it raised) Continuously writes values Faster growth, Slower aging, Youth CA & PA, Prevent retirement, Keep my players happy, My club player recovery, Auto-resolve unhappiness Stops making further changes. Values already written remain in the game Holds a value and restores it Max chairman patience Restores each chairman's original patience while FMAX is open My manager options Become Unsackable and the other four options Built-in game options rather than live tweaks. They write immediately

title: Korean names
summary: Translates English regen names into Korean, along with real players and staff who lack Korean names if you choose. Changes use the game's own naming feature, so they stay in your save.
text: The 'Korean names' screen under Tools on the left, with three switches at the top and the Name list below. This feature only appears when FMAX is set to Korean. What it changes Regens (newgens) in FM27 are generated with English (Latin-script) names. Korean names puts a full Korean name into the player's Common name field (for example, Giacomo Nocera → 자코모 노체라), while leaving their first name and surname in English. Because this is the exact same method Korean name files use for real players, regens look just like real players in-game. - Because names are changed through the game's own feature, they stay in your save. They remain in Korean even if you close FMAX, and show up in Korean in other tools as well. - Anyone whose Common name already contains Korean characters is left untouched. - If a regen originally had a Common name (such as a nickname), FMAX translates that Common name instead. - The 'Current save:' line at the top shows which save FMAX is writing to. How Korean spellings are chosen For each word in a name, FMAX picks a spelling in this order: 1. Your custom spelling (your personal dictionary) 2. A spelling learned from real players’ Korean names from the same country and language 3. Phonetic transcription rules for that language 4. A spelling learned from other countries 5. General rules Every time you open a save, FMAX learns word-by-word spellings from the Korean names that real players have in that game . If your game uses a Korean name file for real players, regens inherit those same spellings. Without such a file, there is nothing to learn from, so only Rule-based spellings are produced. Names changed by FMAX itself are never used for learning. Which language rules to apply is decided from the person's nationality and the letters in their name. Korean names are written surname-first without spaces (김민준), while Japanese and Chinese names follow standard Korean media conventions. Turning it on Auto-translate new regens 1. Turn on the switch. 2. When turning it on for the first time, FMAX asks 'Have you backed up your save?'. Back up your save separately, then click Yes, backed up . 3. FMAX translates English-named regens in the current save in order— starting with My club's players —and continues translating new regens that appear later. Changed names remain in your save. Only names changed by FMAX can be undone with 'Revert to original names'. - Writes names only while the Game date is paused . While days are advancing, FMAX waits and resumes once the date stops. - Scans for new regens once every 7 in-game days, and checks immediately whenever you open the Korean names screen. - The switch applies in any save. Regens generated while FMAX was closed are caught up the next time you run it. - If you turn off Restore previous state on startup in Settings, this switch also starts turned off when you launch FMAX. Also translate real players Translates real players missing from Korean name files (mostly lower-league or smaller-nation players) in the same way. Starts turned off. - Runs after all regens have been translated, and requires the auto-translate switch to be on. - Because many of these names aren't in the dictionary, Rule-based spellings are common. Also translate staff Translates managers, coaches, scouts, and other staff who have no Korean characters anywhere in their name, covering both generated and real staff. Starts turned off, and runs after all players have been translated. Turning off either switch stops further changes for that group. Names already changed remain in place and can be restored together with 'Revert to original names'. Checking progress The line below the switches shows the current status. Status message Meaning Off · n names changed in this save remain in place The switch is turned off Starts once you load a save No save is open in the game Looking for regens Reading players from the game Resumes when the game date stops · n remaining The game is currently advancing the date Game is busy, retrying shortly Automatically retries after a moment Translating · n remaining Writing to the game, with progress shown on the bar All done · Will continue as new regens appear Everything is up to date Running in read-only mode, so nothing is written to the game FMAX is running in read-only mode Stopped because a shared name entry was affected Stopped to avoid changing other people's names along with it. Nothing more will be written until FMAX is restarted The line underneath shows the regen count (and when it was checked), the number of real players and staff without Korean names, changed names, names to change, Unreadable names, and how many people the dictionary learned from. Name list and editing spellings The Name list shows 'Original name → Korean' one person per row, with 'Changed', 'Pending', or 'Leave as is' at the end of each row. - Search: Search in English or Korean. - Filter: All, Changed, To change, Rule-based, My club, Real player, Staff, Unreadable. - Shows 200 people at a time; click Show n more at the bottom to load more. - Spellings with a dotted underline were built from rules because they weren't in the dictionary. Hover over a word to see its language and source (Your custom spelling / Learned from real players’ Korean names / Built from rules (not in dictionary) / Kept as is (non-Latin text)). Editing a spelling 1. Click the Korean word you want to edit. 2. Type the new spelling in Korean. 3. Press Enter or click Save. Press Esc to cancel. Your edited spelling stays in your personal dictionary and is used for every matching spelling in that language as well as future players. If auto-translate is on, players already renamed with that spelling are updated in turn. Clearing the box and saving deletes your custom spelling and returns to the dictionary or rule-based spelling. Revert to original names Click Revert to original names in the top right and confirm to restore original names. - Reverts only Common names changed by FMAX in this s

title: Changing gender
summary: How to change a player's gender to female and use 'Keep men’s team eligibility' so she can keep playing for men's clubs and men's national teams.
heads: 'Keep men’s team eligibility' in Live tweaks
When you need to reload your save
text: Where to change it Change it in Player tab › Info › Gender (Male / Female) under Overview. Always change gender one player at a time from a player tab—backup confirmation and Men’s team eligibility are handled together there. 1. Open a player tab and click Info on the left. 2. Click Gender and choose Female . Directly underneath, a Men’s team eligibility row appears, switched on as 'Keep'. 3. Click Save at the top or press Ctrl+S . 4. FMAX asks 'Have you backed up your save?' for the first time. Back up your save file separately, then click Yes, backed up . 5. Once the 'Name: Female · Keep men’s team eligibility' notification appears, you're done. Gender and Men’s team eligibility are written to the game when you click Save. Gender is part of the game's Player info and stays in your save file. Make a backup of your save before changing it for the first time. Player tab › Info. The Gender field sits inside Overview. Keep men’s team eligibility Football Manager normally bars female players from Men’s clubs and men's National Team squads. Setting Men’s team eligibility to 'Keep' adjusts the game's live rules so that club and national-team eligibility checks—as well as player lists—count her alongside Male players, while her Gender value remains Female. Men’s team eligibility row This row sits directly beneath Gender. Its options are Keep / Never , and the coloured dot beside it shows the live status. Dot Meaning Green Active in the game right now Grey Switched off in Live tweaks, or waiting to apply once connected to the game Orange Could not be applied to the game. Check Live tweaks to see why - Players who were already female in the database (Female players) see this row too. Change 'Never' to 'Keep' and save to make her eligible for men's teams as well. - For a female player already set to 'Keep', you cannot turn this row off by itself. Change Gender above back to Male and save, and Men’s team eligibility turns off with it. 'Keep men’s team eligibility' in Live tweaks In Live tweaks on the left sidebar, look under the Player section for Keep men’s team eligibility . - Lists every player changed to female in the Current save. Each player shows 'Active', 'Applied · Still in the women’s player list', or 'Not in this game', along with an Open button that jumps straight to her Info tab. - A single master switch turns the rule on or off for every listed player. Each save keeps its own player list, while the master switch applies across all saves. - Turning the switch off asks for confirmation and then restores the game's original rules. The players remain female and stay on the list so you can turn the rule back on anytime. 'Keep men’s team eligibility' in Live tweaks, showing changed players and their current status. What the background helper does A windowless FMAX background helper maintains the Men’s team eligibility rules. FMAX launches this helper automatically the first time you change a player's gender or turn the rule on. - The helper reads the player list saved in FMAX and applies the rules to the game whenever the switch is on. - Even if you close the FMAX window, the helper keeps running to hold the rules in place. If you quit and relaunch the game, it applies the rules to the new game session before you load your save, so player lists are right from the start. - After restarting your PC, open FMAX and connect to the game once to reactivate it. - Turning off the switch in Live tweaks tells the helper to restore the game's original rules. - Turning off Restore previous state when reopening FMAX in Settings switches this off and restores the original rules the next time you open FMAX. - If a game update changes the code from what FMAX expects, the helper stops cleanly without applying the rules. It never modifies your save files or your game installation files on disk. When you need to reload your save Football Manager builds its Male players and Female players lists at the moment a save is loaded. If the rules were applied after the save was already open, a player can still be sitting in the women's list. Reload your save once in the game in any of these cases: - A notification or Live tweaks says 'Reload your save once to include them in the men’s player list' - A player's row in Live tweaks reads 'Applied · Still in the women’s player list' - You loaded your save while the helper wasn't running (for example, after rebooting your PC before opening FMAX) - You turned off Keep men’s team eligibility and plan to keep playing Troubleshooting Message on screen What to do The game was busy at that moment Pause the game and try again That part of the game differs from what FMAX expects FMAX may have closed unexpectedly, or another tool may have modified the same spot. Quit the game completely, restart it, and try again Running in read-only mode, so nothing is written to the game Start FMAX normally This game version is different from what FMAX knows Cannot be used until an FMAX update supporting your Game version is released Please change gender one player at a time on the player screen You haven't completed Check backup yet. Change one player in a player tab first to finish confirming Moving to Men’s clubs and call-ups to men's national teams have been verified. Signing contracts through normal transfer negotiations, playing in international matches, and winning awards have not yet been verified to work identically to Male players.

title: Match appearance
summary: Explains 'Appearance' and 'Match appearance' on a player tab's Info page. Match appearance is an FMAX feature for choosing a player's 3D match look—hairstyle, sleeves, boots, gloves, and more.
heads: When changes apply to the game
text: Player tab › Info has two sections that control how a player looks. Section What it covers Where it is saved Appearance In-game player attributes: ethnicity, Hair colour, Hair length, Skin tone, Body Type Written to the game, so it stays in your save file Match appearance 3D match kit & gear: Hairstyle, Sleeves, Shirt tuck, Boots, Gloves, and more Saved only in FMAX, and applied to matches while FMAX is running Player tab › Info. 'Appearance' and 'Match appearance' sit in the middle column. Appearance section Change values just like any other field and click Save . See Editing players for the basics of editing values. Skin tone may appear 1 higher in other editing tools. Values in Appearance only enter the game when you click Save. Match appearance section Pick what each player wears in 3D matches. Every field starts at Game setting , which leaves the game to choose as usual. Field Options Hairstyle Game setting, Bald, Short 1…, Medium 1…, Long 1… Sleeves Game setting, Short sleeves, Long sleeves Shirt tuck Game setting, Untucked, Tucked in Boots Game setting, Boots 1, 2, … Undershirt, Tights, Gloves Game setting, Worn, Never Arm cast, Head bandage, Elbow support, Face mask Game setting, Worn, Never Wristwatch Game setting, Worn, Never Hijab Game setting, Worn, Never (shown for female players only) Available hairstyles depend on the player's gender and whether they are a regen or a Real player. The 'Match appearance' section on the Info tab, with preview thumbnails beside the top four fields. Previews and See all Next to Hairstyle, Sleeves, Shirt tuck, and Boots is a front and back model preview. When set to 'Game setting', it reads 'Auto · Game decides'. 1. Click the preview image ( See all ) to open a visual grid of every option for that field. 2. Click any thumbnail to select it. The picker stays open so you can compare neighbouring styles easily. 3. Click Close . 4. Click Save at the top or press Ctrl+S . Hair and kit colours in the previews are fixed for easy comparison, so they won't match live match lighting. When changes apply to the game Chosen gear only takes effect after you click Save. Changed fields stay highlighted as pending until you save. - FMAX asks 'Have you backed up your save?' for the first time, because it hooks into how the game handles match appearances while FMAX is open. - Once saved, your choices apply to matches for as long as FMAX stays open. Check your updated look the next time you enter a 3D match view. - When you close FMAX normally, the game's appearance handling returns to normal. Your saved looks live in FMAX separately for each save rather than inside the save file itself. text: Installation and running FMAX Do I need to run FMAX as administrator? No. Both installing and running FMAX work without administrator rights—FMAX installs only to your own Windows user account. There is one exception: if you run FM27 as administrator, you must run FMAX as administrator too. Otherwise, the connection badge shows No access . Where do I download the installer? You only need FMAX-setup.exe from getfmax.com. Every time you run it, it downloads and installs the newest version. See Installing, updating and uninstalling for details. Do updates bring new features? Yes—new features arrive in new releases. Every time you launch an installed copy of FMAX, it checks for updates and shows a banner with an Install button when a newer version is available. Clicking Install updates FMAX while keeping all your settings and lists intact. See Updating to a new version. You can check your current version and read the changelog for every release under Tools → Update notes on the left. Do I need to reinstall or set up FMAX again for each save? No. FMAX connects to whichever save is currently open in FM27, whether it's a brand-new save or an existing one. Live tweaks, Locks and favourites are stored separately per save. When you load a different save, FMAX reloads its lists and switches to that save's setup automatically. See What FMAX remembers per save for details. Is FMAX made with Cheat Engine? No. FMAX doesn't use Cheat Engine and doesn't require installing any extra software. FMAX reads and writes values in the running FM27 process entirely on its own. Does it work on Mac or with other FM games? FMAX is a Windows 10 and 11 (64-bit) desktop app. It only reads and writes FM27 version 27.0.1+2503222 , and won't connect to other FM titles or different FM27 builds. What happens when FM27 updates? When the game version changes, FMAX shows Version mismatch on the connection badge and won't read from or write to the game. You'll need an updated FMAX release built for the new game patch before you can use it again. Edited values How long do my changes last? It depends on how you made the change: How you changed it When you close FMAX Saved in your save file? Edit on a tab and click Save Stays as is—the value is already in the game. Yes, once you save the game in FM. ⚡ In-game editor actions Written into the game immediately as soon as you click Apply now in the confirmation dialog, and stays there. There is no undo. Yes, once you save the game in FM. Live tweaks Stops. Live tweaks only run while FMAX is open. Whether changes already made stay behind depends on the tweak. Locks Stops. FMAX no longer holds the value in place, so the game can change it again from then on. Whatever value is in the game at that moment stays if you save in FM. - If you reload your save without saving in FM first, any changes made with FMAX are lost. - Even after you write a value with Save, the game still updates it normally over time—for instance, attributes continue to rise and fall through training and player development. Use Locks to hold a value steady. - Some live tweaks undo their changes when turned off (for example, turning off Max extra staff slots restores only the slots FMAX raised). See Live tweaks for how each one behaves. - When you reopen FMAX, any Live tweaks, Locks and Keep men’s team eligibility that were on when you closed it turn back on for that save according to Restore previous state on launch in Settings (enabled by default). For which changes apply right away and which require advancing the in-game date, see When changes take effect in the game. If I raise CA, do attributes go up automatically? Changing Current Ability (CA) in FMAX only changes the CA number itself—attributes stay where they are. We haven't verified whether the game gradually adjusts attributes toward the new CA later on. Going the other way, if you've edited attributes and want CA to match them, click Set CA to this on the Recommended Current Ability (RCA) card near the top of the Player tab. That sets CA equal to Recommended Current Ability, and still requires clicking Save to write to the game. Recommended Current Ability is calculated from attributes and positions using the exact same method the game uses. CA and Recommended Current Ability (RCA) don't match—is FMAX wrong? No—those two numbers differ for most players inside the game itself. CA is the rating assigned to the player by the game, while Recommended Current Ability is calculated separately by the game from the player's current attributes and playable positions ("for these attributes, CA would be around this"). A difference of 1–3 points is typical; in an actual save, only about one in three players had the exact same number for both. Older versions of FMAX used an approximate calculation for Recommended Current Ability, which could differ from the Game editor by a few points. FMAX now follows the game's own calculation directly. Reload from game (the circular arrow in the tab header) simply re-reads the current values from the game—it doesn't calculate or alter anything. Does the Youth CA & PA live tweak only apply to my club? You choose a target for each rule: All players , Club , Single player , Nation , League or Nationality . While FMAX is open, the rule applies to newly generated youth players matching that target. A 'Single player' rule applies once right away to the player you pick. See Live tweaks for details. Using FMAX with other mods Can I use FMAX with skins or other patches? When connecting, FMAX checks the game file game_plugin.dll . FMAX connects right away if this file is the unmodified FM27 27.0.1+2503222 file, or the original file patched with DoF Patcher. - Patches or skin add-ons that modify this file will trigger Version mismatch on the connection badge.
